definition_zh: 不可避免地；必然地；势必；无法阻止地
definition_en: in a way that cannot be avoided or prevented
core_image: 一块裂开的石碑，裂缝从顶端一路向下延伸，无法停住
scene: 仓库里的货架只用几根细木条支撑，管理员在巡检记录里写下判断。With such thin supports, the shelf will inevitably give way under the weight.
sceneCN: 这里指人力无法阻止的结局（第 2 个义项：无法阻止地）；句意为支撑太细，这个货架在重压下必然垮掉。

pos.zh: 不可避免地；必然地；势必

derivatives.zh: 不可避免的；必然发生的
不可避免的性质（较少用）

senses.title: The announced certainty
senses.definition: used at the start of a sentence to present a result as the predictable outcome of what came before
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，把随后的结果说成前情注定会带来的结局
senses.example: Inevitably, the discussion drifted back to the same old argument.
senses.exampleCN: 讨论不可避免地又绕回那个老话题。
senses.why: As a sentence adverb it colours the whole clause rather than one verb, telling the reader that the outcome was already settled.
senses.whyCN: 作为句子副词，它修饰整个小句而不是单个动词，向读者暗示结局早已注定。

senses.title: No one can stop it
senses.definition: in a way that cannot be prevented by any person or effort
senses.definitionCN: 以任何人都无法阻止的方式
senses.example: With such thin supports, the shelf will inevitably give way under the weight.
senses.exampleCN: 支撑太细，这个货架在重压下必然会垮。
senses.why: Placed before the verb, it claims practical impossibility rather than mere probability.
senses.whyCN: 放在动词前时，它说的是现实中办不到，而不只是可能性很大。

senses.title: Logical consequence
senses.definition: as a conclusion that must follow from the stated premises
senses.definitionCN: 作为由既定前提必然推出的结论
senses.example: If every premise is true, the conclusion follows inevitably.
senses.exampleCN: 如果每个前提都成立，结论就必然随之而来。
senses.why: In logic the word marks deductive necessity, a stronger claim than empirical likelihood.
senses.whyCN: 在逻辑语境中它标记演绎必然性，比经验上的可能性更强。

senses.title: Not necessarily
senses.definition: used with a negative to deny that one thing must lead to another
senses.definitionCN: 与否定词连用，否认一件事必定引出另一件事
senses.example: A wealthy country is not inevitably a peaceful one.
senses.exampleCN: 富裕的国家未必就是和平的国家。
senses.why: Under negation the word stops asserting necessity; the sentence says the link is avoidable, not that it never occurs.
senses.whyCN: 在否定句中它不再断言必然，句子说的是这条联系可以避免，而不是从不发生。

senses.title: As always happens
senses.definition: used of a repeated event that experience makes predictable
senses.definitionCN: 用于经验上早已可料的重复事件
senses.example: As inevitably happens at long meetings, someone raised the coffee question.
senses.exampleCN: 正如长会上一贯会发生的那样，有人提起了咖啡的问题。
senses.why: The habitual frame turns inevitability into a comment on human routine, often with a touch of resignation.
senses.whyCN: 习惯性框架把必然转成对人世间惯例的评注，常带一点无奈。

senses.title: Coupled with something
senses.definition: used before a past participle to say that two things always come together
senses.definitionCN: 放在过去分词前，表示两件事总是同时出现
senses.example: Rapid expansion is inevitably accompanied by administrative strain.
senses.exampleCN: 快速扩张必然伴随行政上的紧绷。
senses.why: Here it modifies a participle rather than a finite verb, describing an inseparable pairing rather than one future event.
senses.whyCN: 这里修饰分词而非限定动词，描述的是不可分离的伴随关系，而不是某一件将来的事。

senses.title: The formal claim of a law
senses.definition: in academic or formal prose, used to present a general rule as beyond exception
senses.definitionCN: 在学术或正式散文中，把一般规律说成没有例外
senses.example: Any measure of this kind inevitably raises questions about privacy.
senses.exampleCN: 这类措施必然引发关于隐私的疑问。
senses.why: The formal register uses the adverb as a rhetorical seal, claiming a general law rather than predicting one case.
senses.whyCN: 正式语域把它当作修辞上的封印，声称的是一条普遍规律，而不是预测某一次情形。

senses.title: Unavoidably incurred
senses.titleCN: 过程中无法免除的代价
senses.definition: used of costs or losses that must be accepted in a process
senses.definitionCN: 用于某个过程中必须承受的成本或损耗
senses.example: Some loss of detail is inevitably incurred when a file is compressed.
senses.exampleCN: 压缩文件时，细节的损失是无法免除的。
senses.why: Technical writing uses the word for unavoidable by-products of a procedure, where no agent is to blame.
senses.whyCN: 技术写作里它指程序中无法避免的副产物，并不归咎于某个人。

intro.en: Inevitably comes from the Latin adjective for unavoidable plus the English adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词的直接来源很清楚：拉丁语「不可回避的」形容词加英语副词后缀。只有英语首见年代是约数，不构成来源争议。

items.en: The verb vitare means to shun or avoid, and it supplies the core of the later adjective.
items.cn: 动词意为「躲开、回避」，为后来的形容词提供词干。

items.en: The prefix e-, meaning out, plus vitare forms evitabilis, that which can be avoided.
items.cn: 表示「向外」的前缀与「回避」合成「可以躲开的」。

items.en: The negating prefix in- turns evitabilis into inevitabilis, that which cannot be avoided.
items.cn: 否定前缀加在「可以躲开的」上，得到「躲不开的」。

items.en: French inévitable and English inevitable carry the adjective into general use; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 法语与英语的形容词把这一说法带入通用语；英语首见年代只是约数。

items.en: English adds its adverb suffix to the adjective, and the new form takes over the sentence-initial role.
items.cn: 英语在形容词上加副词后缀，这个新形式随后承担句首评注功能。

items.en: Modern usage spreads from fatalistic speech to technical and academic claims of necessity.
items.cn: 现代用法从宿命式口语扩展到技术与学术上的必然性断言。

note.en: The first group belongs to the same Latin avoid-root family; the second group names ways of saying that something cannot be escaped.
note.cn: 第一组同属拉丁语「回避」词族；第二组是表达「逃不掉」的近义说法。

entries.definition: Certain to happen and impossible to avoid; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 必定发生且无法避免的；副词的形容词基形。

entries.definition: The quality of being impossible to avoid.
entries.definitionCN: 无法避免的性质；必然性。

entries.definition: Able to be avoided; rare, and formed without the negative prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 可避免的；较少见，未带否定前缀。

entries.definition: The state of being unavoidable, a rarer noun than inevitability.
entries.definitionCN: 不可避免的状态，比必然性一词更少用。

entries.definition: As a logical or causal result that cannot be otherwise.
entries.definitionCN: 作为无法另作他解的逻辑或因果结果。

entries.definition: In a way that cannot be avoided in practice.
entries.definitionCN: 在实际中无法避开地。

entries.definition: As an immediate result, without a separate decision or effort.
entries.definitionCN: 作为直接结果自动发生，无需另作决定或努力。

entries.definition: In a way that cannot be escaped or resisted; literary and formal.
entries.definitionCN: 无法逃脱或抗拒地；书面而正式。

entries.definition: Because circumstances leave no other choice.
entries.definitionCN: 因情形所迫而没有别的选择。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real negative prefix, the real avoid-root and the real sentence patterns.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的否定前缀、真实的「回避」词根与真实句式。

normal.en: The prefix means not and the root means avoid, so the word is simply cannot be avoided.
normal.cn: 前缀表示「不」，词根表示「避开」，合起来就是「躲不开」。

normal.en: Rain does not ask permission before falling, and that is the tone of this word.
normal.cn: 雨点落下前不会征求同意，这正是这个词的语气。

normal.en: Put it first in a sentence and the comma falls like a judge's gavel.
normal.cn: 把它放在句首，后面的逗号就像法槌落下。

normal.en: Under negation it retreats at once: not inevitable means only not necessarily.
normal.cn: 在否定句里它立刻退让：不是必然，只是未必。

normal.en: Engineering reports like it for costs that no procedure can remove.
normal.cn: 工程报告爱用它给无法免除的损耗定性。

abstract.en: Inevitability is not a prediction of a date but an admission that the end was written into the conditions.
abstract.cn: 必然不是预言某一天，而是承认结局早已写在条件里。

abstract.en: The feeling of inevitability comes from looking back, when every step seems to have had no alternative.
abstract.cn: 真正的必然感来自回头看，那时每一步都像没得选。

abstract.en: The adverb quietly moves responsibility away from people and onto the nature of things.
abstract.cn: 这个副词把责任从人身上悄悄拿走，交给事情本身。

examples.en: Inevitably, the first draft raised more questions than it answered.
examples.cn: 初稿不可避免地提出的问题多于它回答的问题。

examples.en: Without maintenance, the pipes will inevitably corrode.
examples.cn: 若不加维护，这些管道必然会被腐蚀。

examples.en: The report notes that some delay is inevitably incurred at every handover.
examples.cn: 报告指出，每次交接都不可避免地产生一些延误。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「因未特布利」——因为没能避开，所以必然发生

root: 拉丁语动词「回避」加表示「向外」的前缀构成「可避免的」，再加否定前缀成为「不可回避的」；英语由该形容词加副词后缀构成。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate sentence-level fatalism, practical impossibility, deductive necessity, negated necessity, habitual resignation, inseparable pairing, formal law-claims and unavoidable process costs.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理句首宿命评注、现实中的无法阻止、演绎必然、被否定的必然、习惯性无奈、不可分离的伴随、书面规律断言，以及过程中无法免除的代价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cracked stone tablet whose fracture runs from top to bottom and cannot be halted.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块裂开的石碑，裂缝从顶端一路向下，无法止住。

branches.en: THE ANNOUNCED OUTCOME: the sentence adverb that declares a result settled.
branches.cn: 宣布的结果：句首副词把结局说成已成定局。

branches.en: THE BLOCKED PATH: no person or effort can prevent it.
branches.cn: 被堵死的路：任何人、任何努力都挡不住。

branches.en: THE LAW-LIKE CLAIM: deductive necessity and the formal assertion of a general rule.
branches.cn: 近乎规律的断言：演绎必然后承与书面语中的一般规律。

branches.en: THE DENIED LINK: under negation the word means not necessarily.
branches.cn: 被否认的链条：在否定句中意为「未必」。

branches.en: THE ACCEPTED PRICE: habit, inseparable pairing and costs incurred by a process.
branches.cn: 接受的代价：习惯性重演、如影随形的伴随，以及过程无法免除的损耗。

intro.en: Inevitably is built from a Latin negative prefix, a Latin avoid-root, two Latin suffixes and an English adverb suffix; every part is transparent.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语否定前缀、「回避」词根、两个拉丁后缀与一个英语副词后缀构成，每个构件都清楚可辨。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family starts from the verb for shun and builds an adjective of possibility, which the negative prefix then reverses.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族从表示「回避」的动词出发，先构成表可能性的形容词，再由否定前缀把它反转。

items.example: The prefix reverses the possibility carried by the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀把形容词所表的可能性反转过来。

items.example: The prefix adds the idea of getting out of the way.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀加上「让开、脱身」的意思。

items.example: The verb supplies the physical image of stepping aside.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「侧身避开」的具体意象。

items.example: The prefixed verb strengthens the act of avoidance.
items.exampleCN: 加前缀的动词强化了「避开」这一动作。

items.example: The suffix turns a verb into a statement about possibility.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成关于可能性的说法。

items.example: The adjective is the positive base that the negative prefix later blocks.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是肯定基形，随后被否定前缀挡住。

items.example: The negated adjective passes through French into English.
items.exampleCN: 带否定的形容词经法语进入英语。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into a manner adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成方式副词。

items.example: The noun names the quality that the adverb asserts.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名副词所断言的属性。

derivatives.zh: 不可避免的；必然发生的

definition_en: at the beginning of a process or period, before later changes
core_image: 一条跑道的起点白线，前方是尚未跑过的路
scene: 项目启动会上，负责人先回顾最早的安排。Initially, the factory produced only hand tools.
sceneCN: 这里指过程刚开始时的情况（第 2 个义项：句首交代最初阶段）；句意为这家工厂起初只生产手工工具。

senses.title: At the first stage
senses.definition: at the beginning of a process, before later changes
senses.definitionCN: 在过程开始时，后来尚未发生改动之前
senses.example: The building was initially designed as a warehouse.
senses.exampleCN: 这座建筑最初是按仓库设计的。
senses.why: Modifying the verb, it fixes the starting state and leaves room for a later revision.
senses.whyCN: 修饰动词时，它固定了起始状态，并为后来的改动留下余地。

senses.title: Sentence-opening frame
senses.definition: used at the start of a sentence to set the opening scene of an account
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，为一段叙述搭起开场的场景
senses.example: Initially, no one believed the rumour.
senses.exampleCN: 起初，没有人相信那个传闻。
senses.why: The sentence adverb organizes the order of events for the reader rather than describing how an action was done.
senses.whyCN: 这个句子副词为读者安排事件顺序，而不是描述动作怎么做。

senses.title: First but not now
senses.definition: used to contrast an early state with a later reversal
senses.definitionCN: 用来把早期状态与后来的反转形成对照
senses.example: She initially opposed the merger, then voted for it.
senses.exampleCN: 她起初反对合并，后来却投了赞成票。
senses.why: The word carries an implicature of change: naming the first position invites the reader to expect a second.
senses.whyCN: 这个词带有「后来变了」的言外之意：说出最初的立场，读者自然会期待后文。

senses.title: At the outset of a period
senses.definition: at the very start of a defined period such as a career or project
senses.definitionCN: 在某段明确时期的最开端，如职业生涯或项目
senses.example: The firm initially employed only five people.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司最初只雇了五个人。
senses.why: Here the word anchors a timeline, often with numbers or dates, and does not by itself suggest a reversal.
senses.whyCN: 这里它锚定一条时间线，常与数字或日期连用，本身并不暗示后来的反转。

senses.title: First step in a procedure
senses.definition: used in instructions to mark the first operation in a sequence
senses.definitionCN: 在说明中标记一系列操作的第一步
senses.example: Initially, the sample is heated to a fixed temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 首先，把样品加热到固定温度。
senses.why: Technical writing uses it as a sequence marker, close to first, with the other steps assumed to follow.
senses.whyCN: 技术写作把它当作顺序标记，接近「首先」，并默认后续步骤会接着进行。

senses.title: Originally intended
senses.definition: used with verbs of planning to describe an intention later abandoned
senses.definitionCN: 与计划类动词连用，描述后来被放弃的意图
senses.example: The site was initially intended for a small clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 这块地原本打算建一间小诊所。
senses.why: With plan, intend or design, the word signals unrealized intention rather than a completed early stage.
senses.whyCN: 与「计划、打算、设计」连用时，它暗示意图没有实现，而不是描述已完成的早期阶段。

senses.title: On first impression
senses.definition: used of an impression formed before closer inspection
senses.definitionCN: 用于尚未细看时形成的印象
senses.example: The poem initially looks like a simple folk song.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗初看像一首简单的民歌。
senses.why: The adverb can mark a first reading or impression that later analysis may overturn.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词可以标记初次阅读或第一印象，而后续分析可能把它推翻。

senses.title: Initial conditions in science
senses.definition: in technical contexts, describing the state of a system at the starting point of an analysis
senses.definitionCN: 在技术语境中，描述系统在分析起点时的状态
senses.example: The model is initially at rest and then subjected to a steady force.
senses.exampleCN: 模型初始时静止，随后受到一个恒定的力。
senses.why: Physics and mathematics use the word for the state assigned at the start of an analysis, a precise technical sense rather than a narrative one.
senses.whyCN: 物理与数学用它指分析起点所设定的状态，这是精确的技术义，而非叙述义。

intro.en: Initially is the Latin adjective for a beginning plus the English adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词是拉丁语「属于开端的」形容词加英语副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The noun initium means a beginning or entrance, and supplies the stem for the whole family.
items.cn: 名词意为「开端、进入」，为整个词族提供词干。

items.en: The verb inire joins in-, meaning into, with ire, to go; literally to go into something.
items.cn: 动词由表示「进入」的前缀与「走」合成，字面是「走进某事物」。

items.en: The adjective initialis, belonging to a beginning, is formed on the noun stem.
items.cn: 形容词由名词词干构成，意为「属于开端的」。

items.en: French initial and English initial carry the adjective into general and technical use.
items.cn: 法语与英语的形容词把它带入通用与技术语境。

items.en: English adds its adverb suffix and uses the form to frame the first stage of an account; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语加副词后缀，用它框定叙述的最初阶段；英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: Modern scientific writing fixes initially for the state assigned at the start of an experiment or model.
items.cn: 现代科学写作把它固定为实验或模型开始时所设定的状态。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin beginning-stem; the second group names ways of pointing to the first point in time.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「开端」词干；第二组是指向时间上最初时点的近义说法。

entries.definition: Happening at the beginning; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 发生在开端的；副词的形容词基形。

entries.definition: The act of starting something or the ceremony of admission.
entries.definitionCN: 开始某事的行为，或加入仪式的入门礼。

entries.definition: The ability to act first, or a new plan set in motion.
entries.definitionCN: 率先行动的能力，或启动的新计划。

entries.definition: To prepare a system or variable for its first use.
entries.definitionCN: 为系统或变量首次使用作准备；初始化。

entries.definition: At the beginning, especially before a change becomes clear.
entries.definitionCN: 开始时，尤指在变化显现之前。

entries.definition: In the first place, before later alteration.
entries.definitionCN: 原本，在后来改动之前。

entries.definition: At the very beginning of an undertaking.
entries.definitionCN: 在一项工作最开始的时候。

entries.definition: Before anything else in time or order.
entries.definitionCN: 在时间或次序上先于其他。

entries.definition: During the first part of a period or process.
entries.definitionCN: 在一段时期或过程的前段。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real going-in root and the real patterns of planning and science.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「走进」词根，以及计划与科学语境中的真实搭配。

normal.en: The root means to go in, so initially names the moment just inside the door.
normal.cn: 词根意为「走进」，所以「最初」就是刚迈进门口的那一刻。

normal.en: Put it first in a sentence and the story is quietly rewound.
normal.cn: 把它放在句首，故事就被悄悄倒带。

normal.en: Say how things were initially and the reader waits for a later turn.
normal.cn: 先说最初怎样，读者自然会等「后来怎样」。

normal.en: In a laboratory report it is the moment the clock starts.
normal.cn: 在实验报告里，它就是计时器归零的那一瞬。

normal.en: With intend or plan it hints that the intention was later dropped.
normal.cn: 与「打算、计划」连用时，它暗示这个意图后来没照做。

abstract.en: The first stage is not yet the story; it is the position from which the story will be measured.
abstract.cn: 最初阶段还不是故事本身，而是后来用来丈量故事的那个起点。

abstract.en: Naming how something began is already admitting that it did not stay that way.
abstract.cn: 说出某事的开始，本身就已经承认它没有一直如此。

abstract.en: An initial state is a clean sheet that later events will mark.
abstract.cn: 初始状态是一张白纸，等着后来的事件在上面落笔。

examples.en: The committee initially approved the plan, then reversed itself in June.
examples.cn: 委员会起初批准了这项计划，六月又推翻了它。

examples.en: The device is initially calibrated at room temperature.
examples.cn: 这台设备最初在室温下校准。

examples.en: Initially, the course was offered only to graduate students.
examples.cn: 起初，这门课只向研究生开放。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「一你手里」——一开始手里什么都没有，只是起点

root: 拉丁语名词「开端」来自动词「走进」，在其词干上构成形容词「属于开端的」；英语经法语借入该形容词，再加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses cover the first stage, the sentence-opening frame, the implication of later change, the start of a period, the first step of a procedure, an abandoned intention, first impression and initial conditions in science.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项覆盖最初阶段、句首框架、后来改变的含义、某段时期的开端、程序第一步、被放弃的意图、初看印象，以及科学中的初始条件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white starting line on a track, with the road still unrun ahead.
core.cn: 核心意象：跑道起点的一条白线，前方是尚未跑过的路。

branches.en: THE FIRST STAGE: the starting state of a process before revision.
branches.cn: 最初阶段：过程开始、尚未改动时的状态。

branches.en: THE NARRATIVE FRAME: the sentence-opening marker and the hint of a later reversal.
branches.cn: 叙述框架：句首标记与「后来反转」的暗示。

branches.en: THE PERIOD OUTSET: the first point on a timeline.
branches.cn: 时期开端：时间线上的第一个点。

branches.en: THE PLANNED BEGINNING: the first procedural step and the intention later dropped.
branches.cn: 计划中的开始：程序第一步，以及后来放弃的意图。

branches.en: THE FIRST READING: first impression and the assigned initial state of a system.
branches.cn: 初次判读：初看印象，以及系统被设定的初始状态。

intro.en: Initially is built from the Latin beginning-stem, its adjective suffix and an English adverb suffix; the parts recur across the family.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「开端」词干、形容词后缀与英语副词后缀构成，各构件在同一词族中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: The family starts from the verb for going in and builds a noun of beginning, then an adjective of belonging to the beginning.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族从表示「走进」的动词出发，先构成「开端」名词，再构成「属于开端」的形容词。

items.example: The prefix gives the direction of entering.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给出「进入」的方向。

items.example: The verb supplies the movement at the heart of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供整个词族的核心动作。

items.example: The noun turns the movement into a starting point.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词把动作转成一个起点。

items.example: The adjective attaches the idea to whatever comes first.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词把这一概念系到最先出现的事物上。

items.example: The verb gives the family its noun of initiation.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词为词族提供「入门、开始」的名词。

items.example: English keeps the adjective for what comes first.
items.exampleCN: 英语保留这个形容词指最先出现的事物。

items.example: The verb is used for starting a process or admitting a member.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词用于发起过程或接纳成员。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into a time adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成时间副词。

items.meaning: the act of setting a starting state
items.example: Computing uses the noun for setting a system to its start.
items.exampleCN: 计算机领域用这个名词指把系统设回起始状态。

definition_en: in a way that belongs to the essential nature of something
core_image: 一块木头内部的纹理，从表面看不见却贯穿整块材料
scene: 果核里的苦味来自它本身的结构，与烹饪方式无关。The bitterness of the kernel is inherently chemical, not a matter of cooking.
sceneCN: 这里指由自身构造决定的性质（第 1 个义项：修饰形容词，指本质属性）；句意为果核的苦味本质上来自化学构造，与烹饪方式无关。

senses.title: By its own nature
senses.definition: in a way that belongs to the essential nature of a thing
senses.definitionCN: 以属于某物本质的方式
senses.example: The material is inherently brittle at low temperatures.
senses.exampleCN: 这种材料在低温下本身就很脆。
senses.why: Modifying an adjective, it says the property comes from what the thing is, not from how it is used.
senses.whyCN: 修饰形容词时，它说明这一性质来自事物本身，而不是来自它的用法。

senses.title: Not by circumstance
senses.definition: used to contrast an internal cause with external conditions
senses.definitionCN: 用来把内部原因与外部条件形成对照
senses.example: The conflict was inherently structural rather than personal.
senses.exampleCN: 这场冲突本质上是结构性的，而不是个人恩怨。
senses.why: The word shifts the explanation from situation to design, and the contrast with rather than is typical.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把解释从处境移到构造上，与「而不是」搭配的对照很典型。

senses.title: Inherently linked
senses.definition: used of two things whose connection cannot be separated
senses.definitionCN: 用于两者之间无法分离的联系
senses.example: Freedom of speech is inherently linked to responsibility.
senses.exampleCN: 言论自由与责任天然相连。
senses.why: In this fixed pattern the adverb marks an inseparable relation, close to by definition.
senses.whyCN: 在这一固定搭配里，副词标记不可分离的关系，接近「按定义就是如此」。

senses.title: No system is inherently safe
senses.definition: used with a negative to deny that a property is guaranteed by the thing alone
senses.definitionCN: 与否定词连用，否认某一性质仅凭事物本身就能保证
senses.example: No encryption method is inherently secure against every attack.
senses.exampleCN: 没有哪种加密方法本身就足以抵御一切攻击。
senses.why: Under negation the word attacks a naive assumption: the thing may become safe, but not by nature alone.
senses.whyCN: 在否定句中它针对一种天真假设：事物可以变安全，但不是单靠本性。

senses.title: Inherently more stable
senses.titleCN: 比较句中的结构性优势
senses.definition: used before a comparative to claim that an advantage comes from design
senses.definitionCN: 放在比较级前，主张优势来自结构本身
senses.example: The arched form is inherently more stable than a flat one.
senses.exampleCN: 拱形结构本身就比平直结构更稳定。
senses.why: With a comparative, the word argues that the difference is built into the structure, not added later.
senses.whyCN: 与比较级连用时，它主张差别已写进结构中，而不是后来附加的。

senses.title: Inherently ambiguous
senses.titleCN: 技术与学术中的固有难题
senses.definition: in technical or academic prose, marking a difficulty that cannot be engineered away
senses.definitionCN: 在技术或学术散文中，标记无法靠工程手段消除的困难
senses.example: Translation is inherently ambiguous when two languages divide the world differently.
senses.exampleCN: 当两种语言对世界的划分不同时，翻译本身就有歧义。
senses.why: The register presents the difficulty as a property of the task, which limits what any method can promise.
senses.whyCN: 这一语域把困难说成任务本身的属性，从而限制任何方法能承诺的范围。

senses.title: Inherently valuable
senses.definition: used in ethics to say that value belongs to a thing, not to its usefulness
senses.definitionCN: 在伦理讨论中指价值属于事物本身，而不属于它的用处
senses.example: The forest is inherently valuable, not merely a store of timber.
senses.exampleCN: 这片森林本身就有价值，不只是木材的储备。
senses.why: Ethical writing uses the word to separate worth in itself from instrumental worth.
senses.whyCN: 伦理写作借它把「自身的价值」与「作为工具的价值」分开。

senses.title: Inherently limited
senses.definition: used of a capacity that cannot exceed what the design allows
senses.definitionCN: 用于无法超出设计所允许范围的能力
senses.example: Human memory is inherently limited in the number of items it can hold.
senses.exampleCN: 人的记忆在能容纳的条目数量上本身就有上限。
senses.why: The word describes a ceiling set by the nature of the system, often with a hint of acceptance.
senses.whyCN: 这个词描述由系统本性设定的上限，常带一点无奈的接受。

intro.en: Inherently comes from the Latin verb for sticking fast inside, through its participle and adjective, plus the English adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「牢牢粘在内部」的动词，经分词与形容词，再加英语副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The verb haerere means to stick, cling or be fixed in place.
items.cn: 动词意为「粘住、附着、固定在某处」。

items.en: The prefix in-, meaning in, plus haerere gives inhaerere, to stick fast inside something.
items.cn: 表示「在内」的前缀与「粘住」合成「牢牢附着于某物之内」。

items.en: The present participle inhaerens, sticking in, becomes the source of the adjective.
items.cn: 现在分词意为「附着于内的」，成为形容词的来源。

items.en: Medieval Latin inheren(t)- supplies the adjective stem used in philosophy and law.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语提供哲学与法学使用的形容词词干。

items.en: English inherent appears in the sixteenth century; the exact first date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语形容词在十六世纪出现，确切首见年代为约数。

items.en: The adverb adds the usual suffix and spreads into technical and ethical argument.
items.cn: 副词加常见后缀，并扩展到技术与伦理讨论。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin sticking-root, including words built with other prefixes; the second group contrasts inherent belonging with value or quality viewed in itself.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「粘附」词根，包括带其他前缀的同族词；第二组对照「固有属性」与「就本身而言」的价值或性质。

entries.definition: To exist as a permanent quality in something.
entries.definitionCN: 作为恒久性质存在于某物之中。

entries.definition: The state of existing as part of a thing's nature.
entries.definitionCN: 作为事物本性的一部分而存在的状态。

entries.definition: Sticking to a surface or to a person or cause.
entries.definitionCN: 附着于表面，或追随某人、某项事业。

entries.definition: Sticking together logically; consistent and clear.
entries.definitionCN: 逻辑上彼此粘合；连贯而清晰。

entries.definition: In itself, considered apart from its use or setting; the emphasis falls on the thing viewed alone.
entries.definitionCN: 就本身而言，撇开用途与处境；重心在单独看待该事物。

entries.definition: From birth or from the earliest nature, often of living things.
entries.definitionCN: 与生俱来地，多用于生物。

entries.definition: Because of the character a thing or person has.
entries.definitionCN: 由于事物或人本身的性格、特性。

entries.definition: At the deepest or most basic level.
entries.definitionCN: 在最深层、最基础层面上。

entries.definition: In its essential respects, when everything secondary is set aside.
entries.definitionCN: 就本质方面而言，撇开一切次要因素。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real sticking-root and the real patterns of blame, negation and technical limits.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「粘附」词根，以及归因、否定与技术限度中的真实搭配。

normal.en: The root means to stick fast, so an inherent quality is glued into the thing and cannot be peeled off.
normal.cn: 词根意为「牢牢粘住」，所以固有属性是粘进事物内部、揭不下来的。

normal.en: With rather than it moves the explanation away from people and situations.
normal.cn: 与「而不是」连用时，它把解释从人和处境上移开。

normal.en: No system is inherently safe is a warning, not a compliment.
normal.cn: 「没有系统本身就安全」是一句警告，不是称赞。

normal.en: Before a comparative it says the advantage was designed in, not added on.
normal.cn: 放在比较级前，它说优势是设计进去的，不是后加的。

normal.en: Ethics uses it to say a thing matters for what it is, not for what it sells.
normal.cn: 伦理学用它说明某物因其本身而重要，而不是因其售价。

abstract.en: An inherent property is the grain in the wood that no surface polish can change.
abstract.cn: 固有属性就是木头里的纹理，表面打磨改变不了它。

abstract.en: Blaming a design instead of a person is a way of saying the outcome was already inside the plan.
abstract.cn: 把责任归于设计而非个人，等于说结果早已藏在方案里。

abstract.en: To call a limit inherent is to stop promising that more effort will remove it.
abstract.cn: 把限度说成固有，就是不再承诺更多努力能把它消除。

examples.en: The task is inherently social, since it cannot be done without others.
examples.cn: 这项任务本质上是社会性的，因为没有他人就无法完成。

examples.en: Some risk is inherently attached to every surgical procedure.
examples.cn: 每台手术都固有地带有一定风险。

examples.en: The method is inherently slow but extremely accurate.
examples.cn: 这种方法本身很慢，却极为精确。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「因黑然特利」——黑在材料内部的性质，从里面长出来

root: 拉丁语动词「粘住」加表示「在内」的前缀，构成「牢牢附着于内」的分词与形容词；英语借入形容词后加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate essential nature, contrast with circumstance, inseparable linking, negated guarantees, structural comparison, built-in difficulty, value in itself, and design-imposed limits.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理本质属性、与外部条件的对照、不可分离的联系、被否定的保证、结构性比较、固有难题、自身价值，以及设计带来的限度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the grain inside a block of wood, invisible on the surface but running through the whole material.
core.cn: 核心意象：木块内部的纹理，表面看不见却贯穿整块材料。

branches.en: THE NATURE: a property that comes from what the thing is.
branches.cn: 本性：来自事物之所以为该物的性质。

branches.en: THE INNER CAUSE: the explanation lies in design, not circumstance.
branches.cn: 内部原因：解释落在构造上，而非处境上。

branches.en: THE GLUE: a connection that cannot be separated.
branches.cn: 粘合：无法分离的联系。

branches.en: THE DENIED GUARANTEE AND THE BUILT-IN EDGE: what nature does not promise, and what it does provide.
branches.cn: 被否认的保证与内置优势：本性不承诺什么，又确实提供什么。

branches.en: THE UNAVOIDABLE SHAPE: difficulty, value and limits that belong to the thing itself.
branches.cn: 无法回避的形态：属于事物本身的困难、价值与限度。

intro.en: Inherently is a Latin in-prefix, a Latin sticking-root and participle ending, plus an English adverb suffix. The same root also builds coherent and adherent.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「在内」前缀、「粘附」词根与分词词尾，再加英语副词后缀构成；同一词根还构成「连贯的」与「附着的」。

latinIntro.en: The root haerere is about clinging; the prefix decides whether the clinging is inward, together or toward something.
latinIntro.cn: 词根的核心是「粘住」；前缀决定这种粘附是向内、彼此相合，还是朝向某物。

items.example: The prefix locates the sticking inside the thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「粘附」定位在事物内部。

items.example: The verb gives the physical image of glue.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「胶水粘住」的具体意象。

items.example: The compound verb makes the attachment internal.
items.exampleCN: 合成动词把这种附着变成内部的。

items.example: The ending turns the verb into a description of a thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变成对事物的描述。

items.example: The participle supplies the adjective stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词提供形容词词干。

items.example: A different prefix gives the English word adherent.
items.exampleCN: 换一个前缀就得到英语的「附着的」。

items.example: The same root with a together-prefix gives coherent.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根配上「共同」前缀，得到「连贯的」。

items.example: The suffix turns inherent into a manner adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成方式副词。

items.example: The noun names the state that the adverb describes.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名副词所描述的状态。

definition_zh: 顺便提一句；附带地；偶然地
definition_en: as a minor or secondary matter, or by chance rather than by design
core_image: 主线旁边的一条小岔路，走进去几步就能回来
scene: 会议记录写到末尾时补了一句与主题无关的小事。Incidentally, the office will be closed on Friday afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里用作句首补充（第 2 个义项：句首旁白，转入次要信息）；句意为顺便提一下，办公室周五下午关门。

pos.zh: 顺便提一句；附带地；偶然地

senses.title: By the way
senses.definition: used to introduce a remark that is not central to the main topic
senses.definitionCN: 用来引入一句与主要话题无关的补充
senses.example: Incidentally, I met your sister at the market.
senses.exampleCN: 顺便说一句，我在市场上遇见了你妹妹。
senses.why: As a discourse marker it signals a change of footing: the following words are an aside, not the point.
senses.whyCN: 作为话语标记，它标示立场转换：接下来的话是旁枝，而不是重点。

senses.title: Sentence-opening aside
senses.definition: placed at the start of a sentence to mark a digression
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，标明接下来是一段岔开的话
senses.example: Incidentally, the museum has extended its hours.
senses.exampleCN: 顺便提一下，博物馆延长了开放时间。
senses.why: The initial position is the clearest signal that the sentence is parenthetical to the larger discussion.
senses.whyCN: 句首位置是最清楚的信号，说明这句话对更大的讨论而言只是插入语。

senses.title: As a side effect
senses.definition: as a secondary result that was not the main purpose
senses.definitionCN: 作为并非主要目的的次要结果
senses.example: The new drainage scheme incidentally reduced mosquito numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 新的排水方案附带地减少了蚊虫数量。
senses.why: Here the word describes a real consequence that came along with another aim, not a conversational aside.
senses.whyCN: 这里描述的是伴随另一目标而来的真实后果，而不是对话中的插话。

senses.title: In passing
senses.definition: mentioned briefly without being made the focus
senses.definitionCN: 简短提及，却不把它当作重点
senses.example: The report incidentally notes a rise in applications.
senses.exampleCN: 报告顺带提到申请人数有所上升。
senses.why: The adverb lowers the information's prominence; the writer does not want it treated as a finding.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词降低了信息的重要性，作者不希望它被当作主要发现。

senses.title: By chance
senses.definition: as a result of chance rather than design
senses.definitionCN: 出于偶然而非有意安排
senses.example: The two researchers met incidentally at a conference.
senses.exampleCN: 两位研究者在一场会议上偶然相遇。
senses.why: This is the older literal sense: an event falls in with another without being planned.
senses.whyCN: 这是较早的字面义：一件事未经计划地与另一件事碰到一起。

senses.title: Parenthetical insertion
senses.definition: used between commas to insert a remark without breaking the sentence
senses.definitionCN: 放在逗号之间，插入一句话而不打断整句
senses.example: The building, incidentally, was designed by a local architect.
senses.exampleCN: 这座建筑顺便说一句，是由本地建筑师设计的。
senses.why: The commas reproduce the spoken lowered tone that keeps the remark outside the main assertion.
senses.whyCN: 逗号复现口语中压低语调的效果，把这句话留在主要断言之外。

senses.title: Secondary relevance
senses.definition: in formal writing, describing a connection that is real but not central
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文字中，描述真实但不居中的联系
senses.example: The clause is incidentally relevant to the question of liability.
senses.exampleCN: 这一条款与责任问题只是附带相关。
senses.why: Legal and academic prose use it to admit a link while ranking it below the main issue.
senses.whyCN: 法律与学术文字用它承认存在联系，同时把这一联系排在主要问题之下。

senses.title: Not the main cause
senses.definition: used of a factor that contributed without being the principal cause
senses.definitionCN: 用于起了作用但并非主因的因素
senses.example: Rising rents were incidentally worsened by the new tax.
senses.exampleCN: 上涨的房租因新税而附带地变得更糟。
senses.why: The word separates accompanying factors from the main causal story, protecting the writer from overclaiming.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把伴随因素与主要因果链分开，避免作者把话说得过满。

intro.en: Incidentally comes from the Latin verb for falling upon, through its noun and medieval adjective, plus the English adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「落到……上」的动词，经名词与中世纪形容词，再加英语副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The verb cadere means to fall.
items.cn: 动词意为「落下」。

items.en: The prefix in-, meaning on or into, plus cadere gives incidere, to fall upon or happen.
items.cn: 表示「落到」的前缀与「落下」合成「落到……上、发生」。

items.en: The noun incidentia names an event that falls upon someone, hence an occurrence.
items.cn: 名词指落到某人身上的事，也就是事件、偶发之事。

items.en: Medieval Latin forms incidentalis, belonging to an incident, as a learned adjective.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语构成形容词，意为「属于偶发事件的」。

items.en: English incidental appears in the seventeenth century, and the adverb adds the usual suffix; the exact first date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语形容词在十七世纪出现，副词再加常见后缀；确切首见年代为约数。

items.en: Modern English splits the adverb between chance events and conversational asides.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个副词分用于偶然事件与会话中的顺便补充。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin falling-root, including a word built with a together-prefix; the second group contrasts side remarks, chance events and true accidents.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「落下」词根，其中包括带「共同」前缀的词；第二组对照旁枝补充、偶然事件与真正的事故。

entries.definition: An event, often a minor or unpleasant one.
entries.definitionCN: 事件，常指较小或不愉快的事。

entries.definition: Happening as a minor accompaniment rather than as a main aim.
entries.definitionCN: 作为次要伴随而非主要目的发生的。

entries.definition: The rate at which something occurs.
entries.definitionCN: 某事发生的比率；发生率。

entries.definition: Two events falling together by chance; built with a together-prefix on the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 两件事偶然同时发生；同一词根加「共同」前缀构成。

entries.definition: A conversational formula for adding a side remark.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中补充旁枝信息的固定说法。

entries.definition: Briefly, while dealing with something else.
entries.definitionCN: 在处理别的事情时顺带地。

entries.definition: Unintentionally, often with the idea of a mishap or error.
entries.definitionCN: 非有意地，常含失误或事故的意味。

entries.definition: As an inserted remark that interrupts the main line.
entries.definitionCN: 作为打断主线的插入说明。

entries.definition: As a remark directed away from the main subject.
entries.definitionCN: 作为偏离主题的一句旁白。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real falling-root and the real difference between an aside and mere chance.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「落下」词根，并区分「旁枝补充」与「纯属偶然」。

normal.en: The root means to fall upon, so an incidental remark simply drops in beside the main point.
normal.cn: 词根意为「落到……上」，所以附带的一句话只是落在主题旁边。

normal.en: Said first in a sentence, it holds up a small sign that reads this way for a moment.
normal.cn: 放在句首，它像举起一块小牌子：这里只是岔开一下。

normal.en: Between commas it is spoken in a lower voice, outside the main claim.
normal.cn: 夹在逗号之间时，它像压低嗓音说出，站在主要断言之外。

normal.en: A side effect is real but nobody planned it, which is the working sense in reports.
normal.cn: 附带结果真实存在却无人计划，这是报告里的常用义。

normal.en: By chance is the older sense: two paths cross without an appointment.
normal.cn: 「偶然」是较早的义项：两条路没有约好就交叉了。

abstract.en: An aside is a way of saying something while pretending not to insist on it.
abstract.cn: 旁白是一种说着某话、却假装并不坚持的说法。

abstract.en: The word lets a writer keep a fact without giving it a place in the argument.
abstract.cn: 这个词让作者保住一个事实，却不给它论证中的位置。

abstract.en: Chance here is not mystery but the absence of a plan.
abstract.cn: 这里的偶然不是神秘，而是没有计划。

examples.en: Incidentally, the train times changed again this week.
examples.cn: 顺便说一句，火车时刻这周又变了。

examples.en: The repair incidentally fixed a small leak in the roof.
examples.cn: 这次维修附带地修好了屋顶的一处小漏水。

examples.en: The two ideas were incidentally connected, not deliberately paired.
examples.cn: 这两个想法只是偶然相关，并非有意配对。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「因此等特利」——因此顺带提一句，只是旁枝

root: 拉丁语动词「落到……上」引申为「发生」，其名词指偶发事件，中世纪拉丁语再构成形容词「属于偶发事件的」；英语借入形容词后加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate conversational asides, sentence-opening digression, real side effects, passing mention, pure chance, parenthetical punctuation, secondary relevance and non-principal causes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理口语旁枝、句首岔开、真实附带结果、顺带提及、纯属偶然、插入语标点、次要相关，以及非主因的关联。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow side path beside a main road, a few steps in and back.
core.cn: 核心意象：主路旁边一条窄岔路，走进去几步就能回来。

branches.en: THE ASIDE: the conversational side remark and its sentence-opening form.
branches.cn: 旁白：口语中的附带补充及其句首形式。

branches.en: THE SIDE EFFECT: a real consequence that came with another aim.
branches.cn: 附带结果：伴随另一目标而来的真实后果。

branches.en: THE LOWERED VOICE: information mentioned without emphasis.
branches.cn: 压低的声音：提及却不强调的信息。

branches.en: THE UNPLANNED CROSSING: two paths meeting by chance.
branches.cn: 未约的交叉：两条路偶然相遇。

branches.en: THE OUTSIDE POSITION: parenthetical insertion, secondary relevance and non-principal cause.
branches.cn: 局外位置：插入语、次要相关与非主因。

intro.en: Incidentally is a Latin in-prefix, a falling-root, a noun and adjective layer, plus an English adverb suffix; the same root also builds coincidence.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「在内、落到」前缀、「落下」词根、名词与形容词层，再加英语副词后缀构成；同一词根还构成「巧合」。

latinIntro.en: The root cadere is about falling; prefixed forms name what falls upon a person, whether an event or a chance meeting.
latinIntro.cn: 词根的核心是「落下」；加前缀后指落到某人身上的东西，可以是事件，也可以是偶遇。

items.example: The prefix shows something falling onto a person or situation.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀表示某物落到某人或某种情形上。

items.example: The verb supplies the image of an event dropping in.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供事件「落进来」的意象。

items.example: The compound verb turns falling into happening.
items.exampleCN: 合成动词把「落下」转成「发生」。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a noun of occurrence.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成表「发生之事」的名词。

items.example: The noun is the base of the medieval adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是中世纪形容词的基词。

items.example: The learned adjective passes into English as incidental.
items.exampleCN: 这个学术形容词进入英语后成为「附带的」。

items.example: A together-prefix on the same root gives coincidence.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根加「共同」前缀，得到「巧合」。

items.example: The suffix turns incidental into a discourse adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成话语副词。

items.example: The noun measures how often an event falls.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词衡量事件发生的频繁程度。

definition_zh: 间接地；迂回地；非直接地
definition_en: by a route or means that involves something else in between
core_image: 两个人隔着一面墙，话从墙上的小孔传给第三个人
scene: 两家公司没有签合同，合作却通过共同的供应商实现。The two firms cooperated indirectly through a shared supplier.
sceneCN: 这里指经由第三方实现（第 1 个义项：经由中介而非直接）；句意为两家公司通过共同的供应商间接合作。

pos.zh: 间接地；迂回地；非直接地

senses.title: Through an intermediary
senses.definition: by means of a person, organization or channel rather than directly
senses.definitionCN: 通过人、机构或渠道，而不是直接进行
senses.example: The disease spreads indirectly through contaminated surfaces.
senses.exampleCN: 这种疾病通过受污染的表面间接传播。
senses.why: The word names a route with a middle term, and the middle term is usually expressed with through.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是一条带中间项的路径，中间项通常用「通过」引出。

senses.title: In a roundabout way
senses.definition: of speech, expressing something without stating it plainly
senses.definitionCN: 在言语上不直说而绕弯表达
senses.example: She indirectly criticized the proposal by praising its opposite.
senses.exampleCN: 她通过称赞相反的做法来间接批评这项提案。
senses.why: In talk the adverb describes a route around the literal words, often to save face.
senses.whyCN: 在谈话中，这个副词描述绕过字面意思的路线，常为了保全面子。

senses.title: By implication
senses.definition: as something suggested rather than declared
senses.definitionCN: 作为被暗示而非明说的内容
senses.example: The report indirectly admits that the target will be missed.
senses.exampleCN: 报告间接承认目标将无法达成。
senses.why: The writer avoids a direct admission while letting the reader infer it.
senses.whyCN: 作者避开直接承认，却让读者自己推出来。

senses.title: As a secondary economic effect
senses.definition: of jobs or income, created through other activity rather than directly
senses.definitionCN: 指就业或收入经由其他活动而非直接产生
senses.example: Tourism indirectly supports thousands of jobs in transport and retail.
senses.exampleCN: 旅游业间接支撑着交通与零售业的数千个岗位。
senses.why: Economics distinguishes direct employment from the indirect work that serves it.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把直接就业与为其服务的间接工作区分开来。

senses.title: Through a chain of effects
senses.definition: as a remote effect produced through intermediate changes
senses.definitionCN: 作为经由中间变化产生的远端效果
senses.example: The factory closure indirectly raised prices across the region.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂关闭经由连锁反应抬高了整个地区的价格。
senses.why: The adverb marks a causal chain rather than a single act, which matters when responsibility is assigned.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词标记一条因果链而非单一行为，这在追究责任时很重要。

senses.title: Not by direct causation
senses.definition: used of a cause that contributed from a distance
senses.definitionCN: 用于从远处起了作用的成因
senses.example: The accident was indirectly caused by poor lighting on the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 这起事故是由楼梯照明不佳间接造成的。
senses.why: Legal and technical writing separates proximate causes from background conditions.
senses.whyCN: 法律与技术写作把近因与背景条件分开。

senses.title: Through an electoral body
senses.definition: of officials chosen by electors or bodies rather than by the whole electorate
senses.definitionCN: 指官员由选举人或机构选出，而非全体选民直选
senses.example: In that system the president is indirectly elected by parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个制度下，总统由议会间接选举产生。
senses.why: Political writing uses the word for constitutional design, where the middle term is an institution.
senses.whyCN: 政治写作用它描述宪制设计，其中的中间项是一个机构。

senses.title: Evasively
senses.definition: of an answer, avoiding the point rather than addressing it
senses.definitionCN: 指回答绕开要点而不正面回应
senses.example: When asked about the delay, the manager answered indirectly.
senses.exampleCN: 被问到延误时，经理绕开正面作答。
senses.why: The adverb can carry criticism: a route around the question is read as evasion.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词可以带批评意味：绕开问题的路线会被读成回避。

intro.en: Indirectly is the negated Latin adjective for set straight, arriving through French, plus the English adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词是拉丁语「被摆直的」形容词加否定前缀、经法语进入英语，再加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The verb regere means to rule or guide, and supplies the straight-line image behind direct.
items.cn: 动词意为「统治、引导」，为「直接」提供直线意象。

items.en: The verb dirigere, to set straight or guide, combines a directional prefix with regere.
items.cn: 动词意为「使成直线、引导」，由方向前缀与「引导」合成。

items.en: The past participle directus means set straight, and English direct comes through French.
items.cn: 过去分词意为「被摆直的」，英语经法语借入。

items.en: The negating prefix plus directus gives indirectus, not straight, hence not direct.
items.cn: 否定前缀加「直的」，得到「不直的」，引申为「非直接的」。

items.en: English indirect appears in the sixteenth century; the exact first date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语形容词在十六世纪出现，确切首见年代为约数。

items.en: The adverb adds the usual suffix and extends from physical routes to speech, causation and institutions.
items.cn: 副词加常见后缀，并从空间路线扩展到言语、因果与制度。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin straight-line root, including the positive and negative forms; the second group names roundabout routes of speech and causation.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「直线」词根，包括肯定与否定形式；第二组是言语与因果上的迂回说法。

entries.definition: Not straight or not direct; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 不直、非直接的；副词的形容词基形。

entries.definition: The use of a roundabout means or an evasive manner.
entries.definitionCN: 使用迂回手段或回避的方式。

entries.definition: Straight, immediate, without a middle term.
entries.definitionCN: 直的、即刻的、没有中间项的。

entries.definition: In a straight or immediate way; the positive partner of the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 以直接、即刻的方式；该副词的反义搭档。

entries.definition: By a long and roundabout route.
entries.definitionCN: 经由漫长迂回的路线。

entries.definition: At an angle; figuratively, in a hinted rather than direct way.
entries.definitionCN: 斜着地；比喻为暗示而非直说地。

entries.definition: By what is suggested rather than stated.
entries.definitionCN: 通过暗示而非明说的内容。

entries.definition: Through another person rather than from the source.
entries.definitionCN: 经由他人而非直接来自源头。

entries.definition: By an unofficial or less visible route.
entries.definitionCN: 通过非正式或较不显眼的途径。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real straight-line root and the real difference between a middle term and an evasion.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「直线」词根，并区分「中间项」与「回避」。

normal.en: The root is about being straight, so the negated form is the path that bends around something.
normal.cn: 词根讲的是「直」，加否定后就是绕过某物的弯路线。

normal.en: With through, the middle term is named: a supplier, a surface, a parliament.
normal.cn: 与「通过」连用时，中间项会说清楚：供应商、表面、议会。

normal.en: In speech it often means the point was made without being spoken aloud.
normal.cn: 在言语中，它常指话没说出口却已经表达了。

normal.en: Economics counts direct jobs and then the indirect ones that serve them.
normal.cn: 经济学先数直接岗位，再数为其服务的间接岗位。

normal.en: An evasive answer is the unfriendly version of the same route.
normal.cn: 回避式的回答是同一路线的不友好版本。

abstract.en: Indirection is how a system hides its middle term inside another system.
abstract.cn: 间接就是让一个系统把中间项藏进另一个系统里。

abstract.en: A chain of effects makes it possible to act here and be responsible nowhere.
abstract.cn: 因果链让人可以在此处行动，却在任何地方都不必负责。

abstract.en: The longest way round is sometimes the only way that keeps the door open.
abstract.cn: 最长的绕路，有时是唯一能保住那扇门的走法。

examples.en: The strike indirectly hurt suppliers far from the port.
examples.cn: 罢工间接伤害了远离港口的供应商。

examples.en: The senator indirectly acknowledged the mistake in her closing remarks.
examples.cn: 参议员在结束语中间接承认了错误。

examples.en: Most of the workers are indirectly employed through small contractors.
examples.cn: 大多数工人是通过小承包商间接雇用的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「因敌若克利」——不直接交锋，绕到侧面去

root: 拉丁语动词「引导」提供「直」的意象，加方向前缀构成「使成直线」的动词，其过去分词为「被摆直的」；否定前缀加在其上成为「非直接的」，英语经法语借入形容词后加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate a middle term, roundabout speech, implication, secondary economic effects, causal chains, remote causes, indirect elections and evasion.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理中间项、迂回言语、暗示、经济次级带动、因果链、远端成因、间接选举，以及回避。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people on either side of a wall, words passed through a small opening by a third hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：两人隔墙，话由第三只手从小孔递过去。

branches.en: THE MIDDLE TERM: a route that passes through someone or something else.
branches.cn: 中间项：经由某人或某物的路线。

branches.en: THE BENT WORD: roundabout speech and its unfriendly twin, evasion.
branches.cn: 弯折的话语：迂回表达及其不友好的双胞胎——回避。

branches.en: THE HINT: the message is inferred rather than declared.
branches.cn: 暗示：信息被推出而非明说。

branches.en: THE DISTANT EFFECT: secondary jobs and effects that travel through a chain.
branches.cn: 远端效果：次级岗位与沿链条传递的影响。

branches.en: THE SEPARATED CAUSE AND THE ELECTOR: remote causation and constitutional design.
branches.cn: 被隔开的成因与选举人：远端因果与宪制设计。

intro.en: Indirectly is a Latin negative prefix, a guiding-root and its participle, a French layer, and an English adverb suffix.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语否定前缀、「引导」词根及其分词、法语层与英语副词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The root regere is about ruling and guiding; the participle directus turns guidance into the image of a straight line.
latinIntro.cn: 词根的核心是「统治、引导」；分词把引导变成一条直线的意象。

items.example: The prefix reverses the straightness claimed by the base.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀反转了基词所声称的「直」。

items.example: The verb gives the family its sense of steering.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词为词族提供「驾驭、引导」的意思。

items.example: The compound verb turns steering into a straight line.
items.exampleCN: 合成动词把「引导」变成一条直线。

items.example: The ending produces the participle behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾造出形容词背后的分词。

items.example: The participle supplies both direct and its negative.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词同时提供「直接的」及其否定形式。

items.example: The negated adjective passes through French into English.
items.exampleCN: 带否定的形容词经法语进入英语。

items.example: English keeps the positive adjective beside the negative.
items.exampleCN: 英语把肯定形容词与否定形式并排保留。

items.example: The noun names the method rather than the manner.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名手段，而不是方式。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into a manner adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成方式副词。

definition_zh: 本质上；内在地；就其本身而言
definition_en: by the nature of the thing itself, considered apart from its use or setting
core_image: 一枚宝石在暗室里自己发亮，不靠外面的灯
scene: 老师提醒学生，读诗不该只为了考试得分。Reading poetry is intrinsically rewarding, even without an exam.
sceneCN: 这里指活动本身带来的价值（第 3 个义项：为自身之故而被重视）；句意为读诗本身就有回报，即使没有考试。

pos.zh: 本质上；内在地；就其本身而言

senses.title: In itself
senses.definition: by the nature of the thing itself, apart from its use or setting
senses.definitionCN: 按事物本身的性质，撇开用途与处境
senses.example: The claim is intrinsically interesting, whatever its practical value.
senses.exampleCN: 无论实际价值如何，这个说法本身就有趣。
senses.why: The word isolates the thing from external purposes and asks what it is like on its own.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把事物从外部目的中隔出来，问它单独来看是什么样。

senses.title: As an essential property
senses.definition: of a quality that belongs to the thing and cannot be removed
senses.definitionCN: 指属于该事物、无法去掉的性质
senses.example: Diamond is intrinsically hard, though a sharp blow can still shatter it.
senses.exampleCN: 钻石本身是硬的，尽管一记猛击仍能把它打碎。
senses.why: Unlike inherent, which stresses inseparable belonging, this word stresses the property viewed in itself.
senses.whyCN: 与强调「不可分离地属于」的固有一词不同，这个词强调的是把性质放在它自身来看。

senses.title: For its own sake
senses.definition: of an activity valued for itself rather than for a reward
senses.definitionCN: 指某项活动因自身而被重视，而非为了回报
senses.example: They study the language intrinsically, not for a certificate.
senses.exampleCN: 他们学这门语言是出于本身兴趣，而不是为了证书。
senses.why: The contrast with external reward is the heart of the word's motivational use.
senses.whyCN: 与外部回报的对照，正是这个词在动机语境中的核心。

senses.title: Intrinsically motivated
senses.definition: in psychology, describing drive that comes from interest or enjoyment
senses.definitionCN: 在心理学中指来自兴趣或愉悦的驱动力
senses.example: Intrinsically motivated students keep working after the task is over.
senses.exampleCN: 受内在动机驱动的学生在任务结束后仍继续钻研。
senses.why: The field fixed the term to separate interest-driven effort from reward-driven effort.
senses.whyCN: 心理学固定了这一术语，用来把兴趣驱动的努力与奖励驱动的努力分开。

senses.title: Intrinsically linked
senses.definition: used of things connected by their very definitions
senses.definitionCN: 指按定义本身就连在一起的事物
senses.example: Meaning is intrinsically linked to use in a community.
senses.exampleCN: 意义与社群中的使用本质上相联系。
senses.why: The fixed pattern says the link is not accidental but part of what the things are.
senses.whyCN: 这一固定搭配说明联系并非偶然，而是事物本身的一部分。

senses.title: Intrinsically valuable
senses.definition: in ethics, valuable without reference to usefulness
senses.definitionCN: 在伦理学中，指不涉及用途即具有价值
senses.example: The wetland is intrinsically valuable, beyond the fish it yields.
senses.exampleCN: 这片湿地本身就有价值，并不只在于它产出的鱼。
senses.why: Moral philosophy uses the word to resist pricing everything by its output.
senses.whyCN: 道德哲学用它抵制把一切按产出定价的做法。

senses.title: Intrinsically unstable
senses.definition: of a system, unstable because of its own structure
senses.definitionCN: 指系统因自身结构而不稳定
senses.example: The reaction is intrinsically unstable and needs constant cooling.
senses.exampleCN: 这个反应本身就不稳定，需要持续冷却。
senses.why: Engineering uses the word for properties that cannot be fixed by better control alone.
senses.whyCN: 工程领域用它指单靠更好的控制也无法解决的性质。

senses.title: Intrinsically safe
senses.titleCN: 本安型的技术固定称法
senses.definition: of equipment, designed so that it cannot release enough energy to ignite a hazard
senses.definitionCN: 指设备经设计后无法释放足以点燃危险的能量
senses.example: Intrinsically safe sensors are used in fuel storage areas.
senses.exampleCN: 本安型传感器被用于燃料储存区。
senses.why: The phrase became a fixed technical label, where the word marks safety by design rather than by added protection.
senses.whyCN: 这一说法成为固定的技术标签，词在这里指「靠设计本身安全」，而不是外加防护。

intro.en: Intrinsically comes from the Latin adverb meaning inwardly, later an adjective, plus the English adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「向内、在内部」的副词，后来转为形容词，再加英语副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The preposition intra means within.
items.cn: 介词意为「在……之内」。

items.en: The old adverb secus means beside, along or otherwise, and combines with intra.
items.cn: 古副词意为「在旁边、沿着」，与「在内」组合。

items.en: Latin intrinsecus means inwardly or on the inside, first as an adverb.
items.cn: 拉丁语副词意为「向内、在内部」。

items.en: Medieval Latin uses intrinsecus as an adjective meaning inner or inherent.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语把它用作形容词，意为「内部的、固有的」。

items.en: English intrinsic appears in the seventeenth century; the exact first date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语形容词在十七世纪出现，确切首见年代为约数。

items.en: The adverb adds the usual suffix and grows strong in philosophy, psychology and engineering.
items.cn: 副词加常见后缀，并在哲学、心理学与工程领域壮大。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin inside-stem, including its opposite; the second group contrasts value or quality viewed in itself with qualities inseparable from a thing.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「内部」词干，包括其反义形式；第二组对照「就本身而言」的价值或性质与「不可分离」的属性。

entries.definition: Belonging to the nature of a thing; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 属于事物本性的；副词的形容词基形。

entries.definition: An older variant of the adjective, now rare.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词的旧式变体，现已少用。

entries.definition: From outside, by external circumstances rather than inner nature.
entries.definitionCN: 从外部、由外在处境而非内在本性决定地。

entries.definition: As an inseparable part of a thing's nature; close, but stressing belonging more than self-view.
entries.definitionCN: 作为事物本性中不可分离的部分；意思接近，但更强调「属于」而非「就本身看」。

entries.definition: From birth or from the earliest nature, often of living things.
entries.definitionCN: 与生俱来地，多用于生物。

entries.definition: In essential respects, setting aside what is secondary.
entries.definitionCN: 在本质方面，撇开次要因素。

entries.definition: Because of the character a thing has.
entries.definitionCN: 由于事物本身的特性。

entries.definition: At the deepest or most basic level.
entries.definitionCN: 在最深层、最基础的层面上。

entries.definition: Considered apart from its relations or uses.
entries.definitionCN: 撇开其关系或用途来考虑。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real inside-stem and the real contrast between value in itself and external reward.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「内部」词根，并对照「自身价值」与「外部回报」。

normal.en: The root says within, so the word asks what a thing is like once you step inside it.
normal.cn: 词根说的是「在内」，所以这个词问的是：走进事物内部后它是什么样。

normal.en: Intrinsic value is what remains when the price tag is removed.
normal.cn: 内在价值就是撕掉价签之后仍然剩下的东西。

normal.en: In psychology it marks effort that continues after the reward is gone.
normal.cn: 在心理学里，它标记奖励消失后仍继续的努力。

normal.en: Intrinsically safe is a technical badge, not a compliment.
normal.cn: 「本安型」是技术标签，不是一句称赞。

normal.en: The word often appears with linked, valuable or motivated, and those partners fix its meaning.
normal.cn: 这个词常与「相联系」「有价值的」「有动机的」搭配，搭档固定了它的意思。

abstract.en: What is intrinsic needs no audience; it is already complete in private.
abstract.cn: 内在之物不需要观众，它在私下里已经完整。

abstract.en: Calling something intrinsically valuable is refusing to let the market finish the sentence.
abstract.cn: 说某物本身有价值，就是拒绝让市场把后半句说完。

abstract.en: The view from inside is not the whole truth, but it is the one the word insists on.
abstract.cn: 内部的视角不是全部真相，却是这个词坚持要看的那一面。

examples.en: The problem is intrinsically difficult, not merely badly explained.
examples.cn: 这个问题本身就有难度，不只是讲解得不好。

examples.en: They value the practice intrinsically, not for the medals it brings.
examples.cn: 他们重视这项练习本身，而不是它能带来的奖牌。

examples.en: The system is intrinsically unstable, so outside control cannot fix it.
examples.cn: 这个系统本身不稳定，外部控制无法解决。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「因吹恩济克」——往里看，性质长在事物内部

root: 拉丁语介词「在内」与古副词「在旁边」合成副词「向内、在内部」，中世纪拉丁语转为形容词「内部的、固有的」；英语借入形容词后加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate self-consideration, essential property, value for its own sake, intrinsic motivation, definitional linking, moral value, structural instability and the fixed safety label.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理就本身而言、本质属性、为自身之故、内在动机、定义性联系、道德价值、结构性不稳定，以及固定的本安型标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gem that glows in a dark room without any lamp outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚宝石在暗室里自己发亮，不靠外面的灯。

branches.en: THE THING ALONE: considered apart from use and setting.
branches.cn: 单独的事物：撇开用途与处境来看。

branches.en: THE PROPERTY: a quality that belongs to what the thing is.
branches.cn: 属性：属于事物之所以为该物的性质。

branches.en: THE INNER DRIVE: value for its own sake and interest-driven effort.
branches.cn: 内在驱动：为自身之故的价值与兴趣驱动的努力。

branches.en: THE GROUND OF VALUE: definitional linking and worth without usefulness.
branches.cn: 价值的根基：定义性联系与不靠用途的价值。

branches.en: THE BUILT-IN CONDITION: structural instability and the fixed safety label.
branches.cn: 内置状况：结构性不稳定与固定的安全标签。

intro.en: Intrinsically is a Latin within-prefix, an old alongside-word, an adjective layer and an English adverb suffix; the opposite is built with a different prefix.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「在内」、古副词「在旁边」、形容词层与英语副词后缀构成；反义词则用另一个前缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The inner word and the alongside word combine into an adverb of inwardness, which later becomes an adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「在内」的词与表示「在旁边」的词合成表「向内」的副词，后来又转为形容词。

items.example: The preposition places the whole word inside a boundary.
items.exampleCN: 这个介词把整个词放进一条边界之内。

items.example: The old adverb adds the idea of a side or flank.
items.exampleCN: 这个古副词加上「侧边、旁侧」的意思。

items.example: The compound first describes direction and then quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个合成词先描述方向，再描述性质。

items.example: The matching outward form supplies the modern opposite.
items.exampleCN: 对应的「向外」形式提供现代的反义词。

items.example: English shortens the Latin adverb into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 英语把拉丁副词缩短成形容词。

items.example: The opposite keeps the same shape with a different prefix.
items.exampleCN: 反义词保持同一形状，只换前缀。

items.example: The suffix turns the Latin stem into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把拉丁词干变成形容词。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into a manner adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成方式副词。

items.example: The rare noun names the quality the adverb describes.
items.exampleCN: 这个少见名词命名副词所描述的性质。

definition_zh: 略微；小幅地；以微弱差距；在边缘地
definition_en: by a very small amount, or at the edge rather than the centre
core_image: 表格边缘栏里只有极窄的一条被墨水填满
scene: 两款耳机听起来几乎一样，评测却给出了细微差别。The new model is only marginally quieter than the old one.
sceneCN: 这里指比较中的极小差别（第 2 个义项：比较句中的「略微」）；句意是新款只比旧款安静一点点。

pos.zh: 略微；小幅地；以微弱差距

senses.title: To a small degree
senses.definition: only slightly, in a way that is easy to miss
senses.definitionCN: 只是稍微，轻微到容易被忽略
senses.example: Prices rose marginally last month.
senses.exampleCN: 上个月价格上涨了少许。
senses.why: The adverb lowers the size of a change without denying it, close to slightly.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词缩小变化的幅度却不否认变化，接近「稍微」。

senses.title: Slightly in a comparison
senses.definition: used before a comparative to mean by a very small amount
senses.definitionCN: 放在比较级前，表示差别非常小
senses.example: The second draft is marginally clearer than the first.
senses.exampleCN: 第二稿比第一稿清楚一点点。
senses.why: With comparatives the word admits a difference while playing it down, often to avoid overstating an effect.
senses.whyCN: 与比较级连用时，它承认差别却把差别说小，常为避免夸大效果。

senses.title: Barely meeting a standard
senses.definition: just enough to count, with little room to spare
senses.definitionCN: 刚够算数，几乎没有余量
senses.example: The candidate was marginally qualified for the post.
senses.exampleCN: 这位应聘者勉强符合岗位要求。
senses.why: The word places the person or thing just inside the line, so the qualification is real but fragile.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把人或物放在线内侧一点点，资格是真的，却很脆弱。

senses.title: At the edge of a group
senses.definition: in a peripheral role or position rather than a central one
senses.definitionCN: 处于外围角色或位置，而非中心
senses.example: She was marginally involved in the project, mainly as an adviser.
senses.exampleCN: 她只是边缘参与这个项目，主要担任顾问。
senses.why: This literal edge sense describes participation at the rim of an activity.
senses.whyCN: 这一字面的「边缘」义描述参与的边缘位置。

senses.title: Near a statistical threshold
senses.definition: in research, describing a result close to the line of significance
senses.definitionCN: 研究中指结果接近显著性界线
senses.example: The effect was marginally significant and needs replication.
senses.exampleCN: 这一效应属于边缘显著，还需要重复验证。
senses.why: Statistics uses the word for a value hovering at the cutoff, a warning rather than a verdict.
senses.whyCN: 统计学用它指在临界线附近徘徊的数值，是警告而不是定论。

senses.title: Of minor relevance
senses.definition: only slightly connected to the matter at hand
senses.definitionCN: 与当前问题只有很弱的联系
senses.example: That detail is marginally relevant to the main argument.
senses.exampleCN: 那个细节与主要论证只是略有关系。
senses.why: The word ranks information near the border of relevance, below what deserves attention.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把信息排在相关性的边界附近，低于值得关注的程度。

senses.title: Barely profitable
senses.definition: of a business or activity, earning only a little more than its costs
senses.definitionCN: 指业务收入仅比成本略多
senses.example: The farm was marginally profitable in a good year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个农场在好年景里也只是勉强盈利。
senses.why: Business writing uses the word for results just above zero, where a small shock could turn loss.
senses.whyCN: 商业写作里它指刚过零点的结果，一次小冲击就可能转为亏损。

senses.title: By a narrow margin
senses.definition: used of winning or losing by a very small difference
senses.definitionCN: 指以极小的差距获胜或落败
senses.example: The motion passed marginally, by two votes.
senses.exampleCN: 这项动议以两票的微弱优势通过。
senses.why: With win, lose or pass, the word measures the gap between sides rather than the size of a quality.
senses.whyCN: 与「赢、输、通过」连用时，它衡量双方差距，而不是某种性质的大小。

intro.en: Marginally comes from the Latin word for edge, through a medieval adjective, plus the English adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「边缘」一词，经中世纪形容词，再加英语副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The noun margo, stem margin-, means edge, brink or border.
items.cn: 名词词干意为「边、边缘、边界」。

items.en: Medieval Latin marginalis means belonging to an edge, especially a page margin.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语形容词意为「属于边缘的」，尤指书页边栏。

items.en: English marginal appears in the late sixteenth century; the exact first date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语形容词在十六世纪末出现，确切首见年代为约数。

items.en: The adjective extends from page edges to effects at the border of notice, hence slight.
items.cn: 形容词从书页边缘扩展到「接近可察觉边界」的效果，因而有「轻微」义。

items.en: The adverb adds the usual suffix and carries both the edge sense and the small-degree sense.
items.cn: 副词加常见后缀，同时承担「边缘」与「程度小」两条线索。

items.en: Modern economics and statistics fix phrases for costs at the edge and results near a threshold.
items.cn: 现代经济学与统计学固定了「边际成本」与「接近阈值的结果」等说法。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin edge-stem; the second group contrasts a small degree, a narrow winning margin and the very different limiting word merely.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「边缘」词干；第二组对照「程度小」「微弱胜差」，以及与「仅仅」完全不同的限定词。

entries.definition: The empty border of a page, or the difference between amounts.
entries.definitionCN: 书页空白边缘，或数量之间的差额。

entries.definition: At or near an edge; small or barely worth counting.
entries.definitionCN: 处于或接近边缘；微小、几乎不值得计入的。

entries.definition: To push a person or group to the edge of influence.
entries.definitionCN: 把个人或群体推到影响力的边缘。

entries.definition: The process of being pushed to the edge.
entries.definitionCN: 被推到边缘的过程。

entries.definition: To a small degree, without saying how close to a threshold.
entries.definitionCN: 程度小，但不说明离阈值有多近。

entries.definition: Only just, with almost nothing to spare.
entries.definitionCN: 刚刚够，几乎没有余量。

entries.definition: To a moderate degree, more than marginally.
entries.definitionCN: 达到中等程度，比「略微」更大。

entries.definition: So small that it does not count as an effect.
entries.definitionCN: 小到不构成效果。

entries.definition: Only and nothing more; a limiter of scope rather than a measure of small size.
entries.definitionCN: 仅仅、别无其他；限定范围，而不是衡量幅度小。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real edge-root and the real split between small degree and narrow margin.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「边缘」词根，并区分「程度小」与「差距窄」。

normal.en: The root means edge, so the word puts the change at the border of what can be noticed.
normal.cn: 词根意为「边缘」，所以它把变化放在可察觉的边界上。

normal.en: Before a comparative it whispers that the difference is real but tiny.
normal.cn: 放在比较级前，它低声说明差别真实但极小。

normal.en: Just inside the line is the situation of a marginally qualified candidate.
normal.cn: 刚好在线内侧，就是「勉强合格」者的处境。

normal.en: By two votes is the clearest picture of a marginal win.
normal.cn: 两票之差，是「微弱获胜」最清楚的画面。

normal.en: In statistics the word warns that a result sits near the cutoff, not safely beyond it.
normal.cn: 在统计学里，它警告结果停在临界线附近，而不是稳稳越过。

abstract.en: The margin is where a system decides whether something counts at all.
abstract.cn: 边缘正是系统决定某物算不算数的地方。

abstract.en: Small differences matter most when a rule turns on a threshold.
abstract.cn: 当规则以阈值为界时，微小的差别才最要紧。

abstract.en: Being marginal is not being absent; the edge still belongs to the shape.
abstract.cn: 处在边缘并不等于缺席，边缘仍然属于这个形状。

examples.en: The two plans differ only marginally in cost.
examples.cn: 两个方案在成本上只有很小的差别。

examples.en: She was marginally faster in the second run.
examples.cn: 她在第二轮中只是稍微快一点。

examples.en: The evidence is marginally in favour of the new drug.
examples.cn: 证据只是略微偏向这种新药。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「马进那里」——只往边上挪进一点点，幅度极小

root: 拉丁语名词「边缘」构成中世纪形容词「属于边缘的」，英语借入后引申出「微小的」义，再加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate small degree, a tiny comparative difference, barely meeting a standard, peripheral participation, a statistical threshold, minor relevance, thin profit and a narrow winning margin.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理程度小、比较中的微小差别、勉强达标、边缘参与、统计阈值、弱相关、薄利，以及微弱胜差。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a very narrow strip of ink filled in at the edge of a table.
core.cn: 核心意象：表格边缘只填了极窄的一条墨迹。

branches.en: THE SMALL CHANGE: a difference easy to miss.
branches.cn: 微小的变化：容易被忽略的差别。

branches.en: THE COMPARISON: slightly more or less than the other.
branches.cn: 比较：比另一方略多或略少。

branches.en: THE THIN QUALIFICATION: just inside a standard or just above zero profit.
branches.cn: 单薄的资格：刚进标准线内，或利润刚过零点。

branches.en: THE RIM: peripheral participation and weak relevance.
branches.cn: 外缘：边缘参与与微弱相关。

branches.en: THE CUTOFF: a statistical threshold and a two-vote winning gap.
branches.cn: 临界线：统计阈值与两票之差的胜局。

intro.en: Marginally is a Latin edge-noun, a medieval adjective suffix, an English adjective and an English adverb suffix.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「边缘」名词、中世纪形容词后缀、英语形容词与英语副词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The noun for edge builds an adjective of belonging to the border, from which English takes both the small and the peripheral senses.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「边缘」的名词构成「属于边界」的形容词，英语由它同时取得「微小」与「外围」两条义。

items.example: The noun names the blank space at the side of a page.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指书页侧边的空白处。

items.example: The suffix turns the edge noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「边缘」名词变成形容词。

items.example: The learned adjective is used for notes written in the margin.
items.exampleCN: 这个学术形容词用于写在页边的注记。

items.example: English extends the adjective from page edges to slight effects.
items.exampleCN: 英语把形容词从书页边缘扩展到轻微的效果。

items.example: The noun also names the gap between two amounts.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词也指两个数量之间的差额。

items.example: The verb turns the edge image into a social process.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把边缘意象变成社会过程。

items.meaning: the process of being edged out
items.example: The noun names the result of the verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名动词带来的结果。

items.example: The suffix turns marginal into a degree adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成程度副词。

items.meaning: the state of being at the edge
items.example: The noun names the state of living at the rim.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名处在边缘的状态。

definition_en: only, and nothing more than what is named
core_image: 一只空盒子，打开后里面只有一张写着「仅此而已」的纸条
scene: 面试官强调，这份工作需要的不是天赋而是耐心。The job merely requires patience, not special talent.
sceneCN: 这里指限定范围、排除更多要求（第 1 个义项：仅仅，别无其他）；句意为这份工作只需要耐心，并不需要特殊天赋。

senses.title: Only and nothing more
senses.definition: used to limit a statement to what is named and exclude anything more
senses.definitionCN: 把陈述限定在所说的内容上，排除更多的东西
senses.example: He is merely a clerk in a large office.
senses.exampleCN: 他只是一家大事务所里的职员。
senses.why: The word draws a boundary around the description and denies any larger claim.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在描述周围画下一道边界，否认任何更大的说法。

senses.title: No more than
senses.definition: used to lower the importance of what follows
senses.definitionCN: 用来降低随后内容的重要性
senses.example: The delay was merely a technical glitch.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误不过是一个技术故障。
senses.why: Here the minimizer deflates significance, telling the listener not to treat the thing as serious.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个「缩小词」给重要性放气，告诉听者不必把此事看得严重。

senses.title: Only a matter of
senses.definition: used before a noun to reduce an issue to one simple factor
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，把问题归结为单一简单因素
senses.example: Success here is merely a question of timing.
senses.exampleCN: 在这里，成功只是时机问题。
senses.why: The pattern collapses a complex situation into one named factor, often for rhetorical effect.
senses.whyCN: 这一句式把复杂情形压缩成单一因素，常带修辞效果。

senses.title: Not merely
senses.definition: in the pattern not merely, used to say something is more than what is named
senses.definitionCN: 在「不只是」的结构中，表示某物超出所说的范围
senses.example: The law is not merely a set of rules but a social institution.
senses.exampleCN: 法律不只是一套规则，而是一种社会制度。
senses.why: Negating the minimizer opens the scale upward; the sentence promises a larger description to come.
senses.whyCN: 否定这个「缩小词」会把尺度向上打开，句子随即承诺一个更大的说法。

senses.title: Merely by doing
senses.definition: used to say that a small action is enough
senses.definitionCN: 表示一个小小的动作就已足够
senses.example: You can sharpen the image merely by changing one setting.
senses.exampleCN: 你只需改动一个设置就能让图像更清晰。
senses.why: The by-phrase presents the minimum sufficient means, with no extra effort implied.
senses.whyCN: 「通过」短语给出最小充分手段，暗示不需要额外努力。

senses.title: Merely because
senses.definition: used to say that a reason is the only one, often to criticize it as insufficient
senses.definitionCN: 表示这是唯一的理由，常含「理由不足」的批评
senses.example: They rejected the plan merely because it came from a newcomer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们拒绝这个方案，仅仅因为它是新来的人提出的。
senses.why: The causal phrase usually carries disapproval: a single reason is treated as too thin.
senses.whyCN: 这一因果短语通常带不赞同：单一理由被视为过于单薄。

senses.title: Merely a formality
senses.definition: used of a step that must be done but has no real effect
senses.definitionCN: 指必须完成却没有实际作用的步骤
senses.example: The signature was merely a formality after the decision.
senses.exampleCN: 决定作出后，签字只是走个形式。
senses.why: The fixed phrase marks a procedure kept for appearance, not for function.
senses.whyCN: 这一固定短语指为了外观而保留的程序，而非为了功能。

senses.title: Downplaying in speech
senses.definition: used in conversation to soften a request or defend an intention
senses.definitionCN: 在对话中缓和请求或为自己的意图辩护
senses.example: I was merely asking, not accusing you.
senses.exampleCN: 我只是问问，并不是在指责你。
senses.why: In speech the word protects the speaker from a stronger reading of their act.
senses.whyCN: 在口语中，这个词保护说话者，免得自己的举动被读得过重。

intro.en: Merely comes from the Latin adjective for pure or unmixed, through French and English, plus the adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; the deeper origin of the Latin adjective is uncertain, and the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「纯粹的、未掺杂的」形容词，经法语与英语，再加副词后缀。直接来源清楚；拉丁形容词的更早词根难以确证，英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The Latin adjective merus means pure, unmixed or nothing but.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词意为「纯粹的、未掺杂的」，引申为「不过是」。

items.en: Old French mier carries the sense of pure or entire into French.
items.cn: 古法语形容词把「纯粹、完整」的意思带入法语。

items.en: Middle English mere means pure or simple, and the modern sense of only develops from it.
items.cn: 中古英语形容词意为「纯粹的、简单的」，现代「仅仅」义由此发展。

items.en: The adverb merely grows out of the adjective with the usual suffix, first meaning purely and then only.
items.cn: 副词由形容词加常见后缀构成，先表「纯粹地」，再表「仅仅」。

items.en: The English adverb is recorded from the late medieval period; the exact first date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语副词见于中世纪末期，确切首见年代为约数。

items.en: The deeper root of the Latin adjective cannot be confirmed, and no confident Indo-European source can be named; this uncertainty concerns the root, not the clear Latin origin of the word itself.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词的更早词根难以确证，无法给出有把握的印欧语来源；这属于词根层面的存疑，而词本身的拉丁来源是清楚的。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin pure-root; the second group contrasts limits of scope with measures of small size.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「纯粹」词根；第二组对照「限定范围」与「衡量幅度小」。

entries.definition: Nothing more than; also, pure and unmixed in older use.
entries.definitionCN: 仅仅、不过是；旧义也指纯粹、未掺杂的。

entries.definition: The superlative of mere, meaning the slightest or smallest.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词的最高级，意为最微小的。

entries.definition: The quality of being pure or nothing but; rare.
entries.definitionCN: 纯粹或「仅是」的性质；少见。

entries.definition: Showy but cheap and false; it shares the letters mer- but not the pure-root.
entries.definitionCN: 华而不实、虚有其表的；只共享开头字母，并非同一词根。

entries.definition: No one or nothing else besides the one named.
entries.definitionCN: 除所说的人或物之外再无其他。

entries.definition: Simply, with no more than the named thing; also used for emphasis in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 仅仅，没有更多；口语中也用于加强语气。

entries.definition: In a plain way, without complication; sometimes close to merely.
entries.definitionCN: 以简单、不加复杂化的方式；有时接近「只不过」。

entries.definition: A phrase that explicitly denies any larger claim.
entries.definitionCN: 明示否认任何更大说法的短语。

entries.definition: Only just, in terms of quantity or degree, not scope.
entries.definitionCN: 就数量或程度而言「刚刚够」，不是限定范围。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real pure-root, the real limiting patterns and the real speech use for softening.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「纯粹」词根、真实的限定句式，以及口语中缓和语气的真实用法。

normal.en: The root means pure or unmixed, so merely strips a statement down to one item.
normal.cn: 词根意为「纯粹、未掺杂」，所以这个词把一句话削到只剩一项。

normal.en: Not merely is the door that opens upward: there is always more to say.
normal.cn: 「不只是」是一扇向上的门：后面总有更多话要说。

normal.en: Merely by changing one setting shows how small the sufficient action can be.
normal.cn: 「只需改一个设置」说明充分行动可以多小。

normal.en: Merely because usually sounds like a complaint about a thin reason.
normal.cn: 「仅仅因为」听上去通常是在抱怨理由太薄。

normal.en: In an argument, merely asking is a shield, not a question.
normal.cn: 在争执中，「只是问问」是一面盾牌，而不是一个问题。

abstract.en: Limiting a thing to its name is a way of refusing to let it grow.
abstract.cn: 把事物限定在它的名称上，就是拒绝让它长大。

abstract.en: The word is small but it draws a hard line around a whole claim.
abstract.cn: 这个词很短，却在整段断言周围画出硬线。

abstract.en: Saying merely is often a way to be modest and firm at the same time.
abstract.cn: 说「仅仅」，常常是既谦逊又坚定。

examples.en: The change was merely cosmetic and fooled no one.
examples.cn: 这个改动只是表面功夫，骗不了任何人。

examples.en: She was not merely tired; she was ill.
examples.cn: 她不只是累了，而是病了。

examples.en: The fee is merely a formality to cover paperwork.
examples.cn: 这笔费用只是覆盖文书工作的形式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「秘而利」——秘密很小，仅此而已

root: 拉丁语形容词「纯粹的、未掺杂的」经古法语与中古英语进入英语，先表「纯粹」，再发展出「仅仅」；副词由该形容词加后缀构成。直接拉丁来源清楚，但其更早词根难以确证，英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate bare limitation, lowered importance, a single-factor reduction, the not-merely expansion, minimum means, a thin reason, an empty formality and polite downplaying.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理纯粹的限定、降低重要性、归结为单一因素、「不只是」的扩展、最小手段、单薄理由、空洞形式，以及礼貌淡化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty box that contains only a slip reading nothing more.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只空盒子，里面只有一张写着「仅此而已」的纸条。

branches.en: THE BOUNDARY: the statement stops at what is named.
branches.cn: 边界：陈述停在所说的内容上。

branches.en: THE DEFLATION: lowering importance and reducing an issue to one factor.
branches.cn: 放气：降低重要性，把问题压成单一因素。

branches.en: THE OPEN SCALE: not merely promises something larger beyond the name.
branches.cn: 打开的尺度：「不只是」承诺名称之外还有更大内容。

branches.en: THE THIN SUFFICIENCY: the smallest means and the weakest reason.
branches.cn: 单薄的充分性：最小手段与最弱理由。

branches.en: THE EMPTY SHELL: a formality without effect and a polite shield in speech.
branches.cn: 空壳：无实效的形式与口语中的礼貌盾牌。

intro.en: Merely is a Latin pure-adjective, a French layer and an English adverb suffix; the deeper root of the Latin adjective is genuinely uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「纯粹」形容词、法语层与英语副词后缀构成；拉丁形容词的更早词根确实存疑。

latinIntro.en: The Latin adjective for unmixed supplies the whole family, and its deeper origin cannot be traced with confidence.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语「未掺杂」形容词提供整个词族，其更早来源无法有把握地追溯。

items.example: The adjective describes wine with nothing added.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述没有掺入别物的酒。

items.example: The noun shows how concrete the image of purity first was.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词说明「纯」最初有多具体。

items.example: A related adjective keeps the same physical sense.
items.exampleCN: 一个相关形容词保留同样的具体含义。

items.example: French carries the sense forward before English borrows it.
items.exampleCN: 法语在英语借入前把这一含义传下去。

items.example: English shifts from purity to bare limitation.
items.exampleCN: 英语从「纯粹」转向「仅仅」这一限定义。

items.example: The superlative survives in phrases about the smallest trace.
items.exampleCN: 最高级仍保存在表示「最细微痕迹」的短语里。

items.example: The rare noun names the quality of being nothing more.
items.exampleCN: 这个少见名词命名「别无其他」的性质。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into a limiter adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成限定副词。

items.example: The adverb is the form that limits a whole statement.
items.exampleCN: 副词形式用来限定整句陈述。

definition_en: in spite of what has just been said; the previous point does not prevent the next one
core_image: 门被风吹得快要关上，门里的人仍把灯点亮
scene: 实验结果不理想，研究者在结论里仍然肯定原假设的部分价值。The evidence was weak; nonetheless, the hypothesis retains some value.
sceneCN: 这里表让步转折（第 1 个义项：尽管如此）；句意为证据薄弱，尽管如此，该假设仍有部分价值。
