forms.label: 分写形式
forms.form: none the less（分写形式，较少用）

senses.title: In spite of that
senses.definition: used to introduce a statement that contrasts with something just said
senses.definitionCN: 用来引入与刚说过的话形成对照的陈述
senses.example: The plan was expensive; nonetheless, it was approved.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划花费很高；尽管如此，它还是被批准了。
senses.why: The word concedes the previous point and then holds the line, a concessive rather than a simple contrast.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先承认前一点，再守住自己的立场，是让步而非单纯对比。

senses.title: Sentence-opening formal link
senses.definition: placed at the start of a sentence in formal writing to mark a turn
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文字中放在句首，标记一次转折
senses.example: Nonetheless, the committee decided to proceed.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管如此，委员会还是决定继续推进。
senses.why: Heavy connectors at the start of a sentence belong to written argument; speech usually prefers but or still.
senses.whyCN: 句首的厚重连接词属于书面论证；口语通常更爱用「但是」或「仍然」。

senses.title: Mid-sentence parenthesis
senses.definition: set between commas after the subject to concede without stopping the sentence
senses.definitionCN: 放在主语后的逗号之间，作出让步却不打断句子
senses.example: The method, nonetheless, produced reliable results.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方法尽管如此，仍产生了可靠的结果。
senses.why: The parenthetical position lowers the contrast's volume while keeping it visible.
senses.whyCN: 插入语位置降低了转折的音量，却仍让它可见。

senses.title: Still true
senses.definition: used after a fact to insist that another fact remains true
senses.definitionCN: 在一个事实之后坚持另一个事实仍然成立
senses.example: The theory is old; nonetheless, it remains useful.
senses.exampleCN: 这个理论很旧；尽管如此，它仍然有用。
senses.why: The word defends a surviving claim against the pressure of the preceding objection.
senses.whyCN: 这个词为仍然存活的说法辩护，顶住前面反对意见的压力。

senses.title: Nonetheless + comparative
senses.definition: used before a comparative to say a quality survives a counterargument
senses.definitionCN: 放在比较级前，表示某种优点在反驳之后仍然存在
senses.example: The second route is longer but nonetheless safer.
senses.exampleCN: 第二条路线更长，尽管如此却更安全。
senses.why: With a comparative, the word admits a drawback and then advances a compensating advantage.
senses.whyCN: 与比较级连用时，它承认一个缺点，再提出补偿性的优点。

senses.title: Concessive academic hedging
senses.definition: in academic prose, acknowledging a limitation before restating the main claim
senses.definitionCN: 在学术散文中，先承认局限，再重述主要论点
senses.example: The sample is small; nonetheless, the pattern is suggestive.
senses.exampleCN: 样本很小；尽管如此，这一模式仍能提供线索。
senses.why: The register uses the word to show balance: a weakness is named so that the claim can stand on narrower ground.
senses.whyCN: 这一语域用它显示平衡：先点出弱点，让论点站在更窄的地面上。

senses.title: Conjunctive-adverb grammar
senses.definition: linking two independent clauses without acting as a conjunction
senses.definitionCN: 连接两个独立分句，却不充当连词
senses.example: The cost was high; the project was nonetheless completed.
senses.exampleCN: 成本很高；这个项目尽管如此还是完成了。
senses.why: The word can sit after the subject and needs a semicolon or full stop before it, unlike the conjunction but.
senses.whyCN: 它可以放在主语之后，前面需要分号或句号，这一点与连词「但是」不同。

senses.title: A restrained however
senses.definition: as a restrained alternative to however when the contrast is partial
senses.definitionCN: 当对照只是部分成立时，作为比「然而」更克制的替代
senses.example: The design is not original; it is nonetheless effective.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计并不新颖；尽管如此，它仍然有效。
senses.why: The word concedes more than however usually does and claims survival rather than reversal.
senses.whyCN: 它比「然而」通常所作的让步更多，主张的是「存活」而不是「反转」。

intro.en: Nonetheless is a native English compound of none, the and less. There is no Latin element in its history, and its construction is fully transparent.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语本族语的复合词，由「没有一个」「这个」与「更少」三部分组成。它的历史中没有拉丁语成分，构词完全透明。

items.en: The negative pronoun nan, ancestor of none, means not one.
items.cn: 否定代词，意为「没有一个」，是现代对应词的前身。

items.en: The comparative laessa, ancestor of less, means smaller in amount.
items.cn: 比较级，意为「更少」，是现代对应词的前身。

items.en: Middle English none the less literally means not the less, that is, no smaller in degree.
items.cn: 中古英语字面意为「不因此更少」，即程度不减。

items.en: The phrase hardens into a single concessive adverb in early modern English.
items.cn: 这一短语在近代早期凝固为单个让步副词。

items.en: The modern spelling is usually written as one word; the first date of the fused form is approximate.
items.cn: 现代拼写通常合为一词；合写形式的首见年代为约数。

items.en: The connector settles into formal and academic prose, where a heavier link suits the argument.
items.cn: 这个连接词定居于正式与学术散文，较重的衔接更适合论证。

note.en: The first group contains near-twin connectors and the components of the compound; the second group contrasts concessive links with plainer ones.
note.cn: 第一组是同义的「双胞胎」连接词与本复合词的构件；第二组对照让步连接词与更朴素的转折说法。

entries.definition: In spite of that; built with never rather than none, and slightly more formal in feel.
entries.definitionCN: 尽管如此；首元素由「从不」构成而非「没有一个」，语感略正式。

entries.definition: The separated spelling of the same phrase, now less common.
entries.definitionCN: 同一短语的分写形式，现在较少见。

entries.definition: To make or become smaller, built on the same comparative stem.
entries.definitionCN: 使变小；由同一比较级词干构成。

entries.definition: Smaller in size or importance; a comparative adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 在大小或重要性上更小的；比较级形容词。

entries.definition: A plainer contrast marker that can introduce a full reversal.
entries.definitionCN: 更朴素的转折标记，可引出完全的反转。

entries.definition: Even so; used in speech where nonetheless would sound heavy.
entries.definitionCN: 即使如此；用于口语，而「尽管如此」会显得重。

entries.definition: A conversational concessive phrase with the same core meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 口语让步短语，核心意思相同。

entries.definition: A short concessive conjunction or adverb, often literary.
entries.definitionCN: 简短的让步连词或副词，常带书面色彩。

entries.definition: A heavier formal preposition or adverb meaning in spite of.
entries.definitionCN: 更重的正式介词或副词，意为「尽管」。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real three-part construction and the real split between formal and spoken registers.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的三段式构造，并区分正式语域与口语语域。

normal.en: The phrase literally says not the less, so the amount does not shrink.
normal.cn: 字面说的是「不因此更少」，所以分量没有缩减。

normal.en: Say it at the start of a sentence in an essay and it sounds like a formal nod.
normal.cn: 在文章句首说它，听上去像正式地点一下头。

normal.en: Between commas it concedes in a lower voice.
normal.cn: 夹在逗号之间时，它用较低的声音作出让步。

normal.en: With but it doubles the signal: but nonetheless is a common pair.
normal.cn: 与「但是」连用会加倍信号：「但仍然」是常见搭配。

normal.en: In speech, still or even so usually does the same work with less weight.
normal.cn: 口语里，用「仍然」或「即使如此」往往更轻便。

abstract.en: A concession is not a surrender; it is a way of keeping the claim standing after a blow.
abstract.cn: 让步不是投降，而是在受击之后让主张继续站住。

abstract.en: The word builds a bridge that admits the wind but still carries the walker.
abstract.cn: 这个词搭起一座桥：承认有风，却仍把行人送过去。

abstract.en: Formal argument needs a heavier hinge because the door it holds open is heavier.
abstract.cn: 正式论证需要更重的铰链，因为它要撑住的门更重。

examples.en: The weather was poor; nonetheless, the match went ahead.
examples.cn: 天气很差；尽管如此，比赛还是照常进行。

examples.en: The claims are old, but nonetheless worth testing.
examples.cn: 这些说法很旧，但仍然值得检验。

examples.en: Nonetheless, the results do not support a firm conclusion.
examples.cn: 尽管如此，这些结果并不支持一个确定的结论。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「难则勒斯」——再难也不因此减少，仍然如此

root: 由英语本族语的「没有一个」「这个」与「更少」三部分合成，字面意为「不因此更少」，中古英语时期凝固为让步副词。构词完全透明，不涉及拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate bare concession, sentence-opening formality, parenthetical lowering, surviving truth, comparative compensation, academic balance, conjunctive-adverb grammar and restrained contrast.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理单纯让步、句首正式衔接、插入语降调、仍成立的真相、比较中的补偿、学术平衡、连接副词语法，以及收敛的转折。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door nearly shut by wind, while the person inside still lights the lamp.
core.cn: 核心意象：门被风吹得快要关上，门里的人仍把灯点亮。

branches.en: THE CONCESSION: the previous point is admitted, not cancelled.
branches.cn: 让步：前一点被承认，而不是被取消。

branches.en: THE HINGE: the formal sentence-opening link and its quiet parenthetical form.
branches.cn: 铰链：句首的正式衔接及其安静的插入形式。

branches.en: THE SURVIVING CLAIM: truth that outlasts objection, and academic balance.
branches.cn: 存活的主张：熬过反驳的真相，以及学术上的平衡。

branches.en: THE COMPENSATION: a drawback admitted, an advantage advanced.
branches.cn: 补偿：承认缺点，再提出优点。

branches.en: THE GRAMMAR AND THE TONE: adverb not conjunction, and a milder however.
branches.cn: 语法与语气：副词而非连词，以及更温和的转折说法。

intro.en: Nonetheless has no Latin element at all; it is a native compound of a negative pronoun, a definite article and a comparative, later fused into one adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词完全没有拉丁语成分；它由否定代词、定冠词与比较级合成的本族语复合词，后来熔合成一个副词。

latinIntro.en: There are no Latin entries for this word. The forms below are native English and Old English pieces, and they are the true parts of the compound.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语构件。下面列出的都是英语与古英语成分，它们才是这个复合词的真实构件。

items.structure: English pronoun, from Old English nan
items.example: The first element denies the amount outright.
items.exampleCN: 第一个成分直接否认数量。

items.example: The article holds the comparison in place.
items.exampleCN: 冠词把比较关系固定住。

items.example: The comparative supplies the scale that is being denied.
items.exampleCN: 比较级提供被否定的那个刻度。

items.example: The adjective is a cousin of the same comparative stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是同一比较级词干的表亲。

items.example: The verb turns the comparative into an action.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把比较级变成动作。

items.example: The separated phrase is the direct ancestor of the fused adverb.
items.exampleCN: 分写短语是合写副词的直接前身。

items.example: The fused form works as a single concessive link.
items.exampleCN: 合写形式作为单个让步连接词使用。

items.example: The parallel form swaps the first element and keeps the same frame.
items.exampleCN: 平行形式换掉首元素，保留同一框架。

items.example: A heavier formal rival covers the same ground.
items.exampleCN: 一个更重的正式对手覆盖同一意义范围。

definition_zh: 尤其；显著地；值得注意的是
definition_en: especially, or in a way that is easy to notice
core_image: 一群人中只有一个人穿亮色外套，视线自然落在他身上
scene: 报告在列举增长地区时，特别点出了一个省。Several provinces grew, notably the coastal one.
sceneCN: 这里指从一组中特别举出一项（第 3 个义项：举出突出例子）；句意为几个省都有增长，尤其是沿海那个省。

pos.zh: 尤其；显著地；值得注意的是

senses.title: Especially
senses.definition: more than others, in a way that deserves attention
senses.definitionCN: 比其余更突出，值得注意
senses.example: The region is notably dry in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区夏季格外干燥。
senses.why: The adverb raises one item above its neighbours without saying it is the only one.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词把某一项抬到邻项之上，却不说它是唯一的一项。

senses.title: Sentence-opening highlight
senses.definition: at the start of a sentence, drawing attention to the fact that follows
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，把注意力引向随后的事实
senses.example: Notably, no one objected to the change.
senses.exampleCN: 值得注意的是，没有人反对这一改动。
senses.why: The initial position tells the reader that the next clause is the point worth remembering.
senses.whyCN: 句首位置告诉读者，下一个小句才是值得记住的要点。

senses.title: Introducing a striking example
senses.definition: used before a noun phrase to single out an example
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词短语前，单举一个例子
senses.example: Some countries, notably Germany, changed their policy.
senses.exampleCN: 一些国家，尤其是德国，改变了政策。
senses.why: The word introduces a specimen that makes the general claim concrete.
senses.whyCN: 这个词引出一个样本，使一般性说法变得具体。

senses.title: To a noticeable degree
senses.definition: used before an adjective to say a quality is easy to observe
senses.definitionCN: 放在形容词前，表示某种性质容易观察到
senses.example: The two versions are notably different in tone.
senses.exampleCN: 两个版本在语气上明显不同。
senses.why: Here it modifies an adjective and measures visibility, close to noticeably.
senses.whyCN: 这里修饰形容词，衡量的是「可见程度」，接近「明显地」。

senses.title: Notably absent
senses.definition: in the fixed pattern notably absent, conspicuous by not being there
senses.definitionCN: 在固定搭配「显著缺席」中，指因不在场而引人注意
senses.example: Notably absent from the report was any mention of cost.
senses.exampleCN: 报告中明显缺席的是任何关于成本的提及。
senses.why: The phrase turns absence itself into the noticeable fact, a common rhetorical move.
senses.whyCN: 这一短语把「缺席」本身变成引人注意的事实，是常见的修辞手法。

senses.title: Before a comparative
senses.definition: used with a comparative to mark a difference larger than expected
senses.definitionCN: 与比较级连用，标记超出预期的差距
senses.example: This year's harvest was notably better than last year's.
senses.exampleCN: 今年的收成明显好于去年。
senses.why: With comparatives the word enlarges the gap rather than merely reporting it.
senses.whyCN: 与比较级连用时，它放大差距，而不只是报告差距。

senses.title: Academic evidence marker
senses.titleCN: 学术写作中的证据标记
senses.definition: in research writing, flagging the observation that carries the argument
senses.definitionCN: 在研究写作中，标出支撑论证的那项观察
senses.example: The study found, notably, that older users adapted faster.
senses.exampleCN: 研究发现，值得注意的是，年长用户适应得更快。
senses.why: The marker tells readers which result the author treats as decisive.
senses.whyCN: 这个标记告诉读者，作者把哪一项结果当作关键。

senses.title: In a way that attracts notice
senses.definition: of behaviour or appearance, in a manner that draws attention
senses.definitionCN: 指行为或外表以引人注意的方式
senses.example: The house was notably decorated for the festival.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋房子为节日做了惹眼的装饰。
senses.why: The older manner sense describes doing something in a way that is meant to be seen.
senses.whyCN: 较早的方式义描述以「就是要被看见」的方式做事。

intro.en: Notably comes from the Latin adjective for worthy of note, through French, plus the English adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「值得注意的」形容词，经法语，再加英语副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The noun nota means a mark, sign or written note.
items.cn: 名词意为「记号、标记、注记」。

items.en: The verb notare means to mark or observe, and gives the stem of the adjective.
items.cn: 动词意为「标记、注意」，提供形容词词干。

items.en: The adjective notabilis means worthy of note or remarkable.
items.cn: 形容词意为「值得注意的、显著的」。

items.en: Old French notable and English notable carry the adjective into use.
items.cn: 古法语与英语形容词把它带入使用。

items.en: The adverb adds the usual suffix; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 副词加常见后缀；英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: Modern prose uses notably both to single out examples and to measure visible degree.
items.cn: 现代散文既用它单举例子，也用它衡量可见的程度。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin mark-root; the second group contrasts highlighting an example with intensifying a degree.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「记号」词根；第二组对照「举出例子」与「加强程度」。

entries.definition: Worthy of attention; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 值得注意的；副词的形容词基形。

entries.definition: The state of being important enough to be noticed.
entries.definitionCN: 重要到足以被注意的状态。

entries.definition: A system of written marks or symbols.
entries.definitionCN: 书写的记号或符号系统。

entries.definition: To mark something with symbols or notes.
entries.definitionCN: 用符号或注记标出某物。

entries.definition: Above all, or to a high degree; broader than notably because it also intensifies.
entries.definitionCN: 首先、格外；比「值得注意的是」更宽，因为它也能单纯加强程度。

entries.definition: Specifically or especially; often narrower and more precise than especially.
entries.definitionCN: 具体地或尤其；常比「尤其」更窄、更精确。

entries.definition: In a surprising or striking degree.
entries.definitionCN: 以达到令人惊讶或醒目的程度。

entries.definition: In a way that is clearly visible or attracting attention.
entries.definitionCN: 以清楚可见或引人注意的方式。

entries.definition: A phrase singling out one member of a group.
entries.definitionCN: 从一组中单举一个成员的说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real mark-root and the real split between singling out an example and measuring degree.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「记号」词根，并区分「单举例子」与「衡量程度」。

normal.en: The root is a mark, so notably points to the item with a mark beside it.
normal.cn: 词根是「记号」，所以这个词指向旁边打了记号的那一项。

normal.en: Notably absent is a sentence about what is not there, which makes the gap loud.
normal.cn: 「显著缺席」说的是不在场的东西，反而让空缺更响。

normal.en: Before a comparative it says the gap is bigger than you might assume.
normal.cn: 放在比较级前，它说明差距比你以为的更大。

normal.en: In academic prose it quietly tells the reader which result matters.
normal.cn: 在学术文字里，它悄悄告诉读者哪项结果才重要。

normal.en: Most notably often opens a list that ends with the strongest case.
normal.cn: 「最值得注意的是」常引出一个以最强例子收尾的清单。

abstract.en: A mark on a page is a promise that this part will be looked at twice.
abstract.cn: 纸上的记号是一种承诺：这一处会被再看一眼。

abstract.en: Attention is a scarce resource, and the word spends it on one item.
abstract.cn: 注意力是稀缺资源，这个词把它花在其中一项上。

abstract.en: Saying what is notably absent is a way of describing a room by its missing chair.
abstract.cn: 说某物显著缺席，就是靠少了一把椅子来描述一间屋子。

examples.en: The team improved, notably in defence.
examples.cn: 球队进步了，尤其是在防守方面。

examples.en: Notably, the two accounts disagree on the date.
examples.cn: 值得注意的是，两份记载在日期上并不一致。

examples.en: The second method is notably cheaper to run.
examples.cn: 第二种方法运行起来明显更便宜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「诺特布利」——被特别记在备忘录上，所以显著

root: 拉丁语名词「记号」派生动词「标记、注意」，再构成形容词「值得注意的」；英语经法语借入形容词后加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate emphasis above neighbours, sentence-opening highlight, a singled-out example, visible degree, conspicuous absence, enlarged comparison, academic evidence marking and attention-drawing manner.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理高于邻项的强调、句首提示、单举例子、可见程度、显著缺席、放大的比较、学术证据标记，以及引人注意的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one bright coat in a crowd, pulling every glance toward it.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群里一件亮色外套，把视线都拉过去。

branches.en: THE RAISED ITEM: one thing stands above its neighbours.
branches.cn: 被抬高的一项：某物高于邻项。

branches.en: THE FLAG: the sentence-opening highlight and the academic evidence marker.
branches.cn: 旗标：句首提示与学术证据标记。

branches.en: THE EXAMPLE: a specimen that makes the general claim concrete.
branches.cn: 例子：使一般说法具体化的样本。

branches.en: THE MEASURED DEGREE: visible quality and an enlarged comparison.
branches.cn: 可测的程度：可见的性质与被放大的比较。

branches.en: THE NOTICED ABSENCE AND MANNER: the gap heard loud, and behaviour meant to be seen.
branches.cn: 被注意的空缺与方式：响亮的缺席，以及有意被看见的举止。

intro.en: Notably is a Latin mark-noun, a Latin verb stem, an adjective suffix, a French layer and an English adverb suffix.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「记号」名词、「标记」动词词干、形容词后缀、法语层与英语副词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The noun for a mark builds a verb of marking and an adjective of being worth a mark, from which English takes the adverb.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「记号」的名词构成「标记」动词与「值得被标记」的形容词，英语由它取得副词。

items.example: The noun is the concrete mark that starts the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是词族起点的具体记号。

items.example: The verb turns the mark into an act of noticing.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把记号变成「注意到」的动作。

items.example: The suffix builds an adjective of worthiness.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表「值得」的形容词。

items.example: The adjective says a thing deserves a mark beside it.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词说某物值得在旁边打个记号。

items.example: English keeps the adjective for people and events worth attention.
items.exampleCN: 英语保留这个形容词，用于值得注意的人与事。

items.example: The noun names the social result of being noticed.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名被注意带来的社会结果。

items.example: A different branch of the family names written symbols.
items.exampleCN: 词族的另一支命名书写的符号。

items.example: The verb returns to the physical act of marking.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词回到「做记号」的具体动作。

items.example: The suffix turns notable into a highlighting adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成提示性副词。

definition_en: sometimes, but not often, and without a regular pattern
core_image: 一本日历上零星画着几个小圈，多数日子空白
scene: 老式收音机会在深夜突然冒出杂音。The old radio occasionally crackles late at night.
sceneCN: 这里指不规律地偶尔发生（第 3 个义项：以不规则间隔出现）；句意为这台旧收音机深夜偶尔会噼啪作响。

senses.title: Sometimes but not often
senses.definition: at times, with long gaps between occurrences
senses.definitionCN: 有时发生，但两次之间间隔较长
senses.example: I occasionally walk to work when the weather is fine.
senses.exampleCN: 天气好的时候，我偶尔步行去上班。
senses.why: The adverb sits on the lower part of the frequency scale, below sometimes and well below often.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词处在频率刻度的较低位置，低于「有时」，远低于「经常」。

senses.title: Sentence-opening frequency frame
senses.definition: at the start of a sentence, setting a sporadic pattern
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，为整句设定「零星发生」的模式
senses.example: Occasionally, the system fails without any warning.
senses.exampleCN: 偶尔，系统会在毫无预警的情况下失灵。
senses.why: The front position frames the whole event as an exception to the normal case.
senses.whyCN: 句首位置把整个事件框成正常情形之外的例外。

senses.title: At irregular intervals
senses.definition: happening without a fixed schedule or pattern
senses.definitionCN: 没有固定时间表或规律地发生
senses.example: The machine occasionally jams during heavy use.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器在高负荷使用时会偶尔卡住。
senses.why: The word denies regularity: the events happen, but no rhythm can be predicted.
senses.whyCN: 这个词否认规律性：事情会发生，却预测不出节奏。

senses.title: Now and then in speech
senses.definition: used in relaxed speech for an activity done from time to time
senses.definitionCN: 在轻松口语中指不时做一次的活动
senses.example: We occasionally meet for coffee after work.
senses.exampleCN: 我们下班后偶尔一起喝杯咖啡。
senses.why: The conversational register makes the word a soft way to describe a loose habit.
senses.whyCN: 口语语域让这个词成为描述松散习惯的柔和说法。

senses.title: Sporadic in technical writing
senses.definition: of faults or events that appear intermittently under certain conditions
senses.definitionCN: 指故障或事件在特定条件下间歇出现
senses.example: Errors occur occasionally when the load exceeds the limit.
senses.exampleCN: 当负载超过上限时，错误会偶尔出现。
senses.why: Technical reports use the word to admit a fault without claiming it is constant or reproducible.
senses.whyCN: 技术报告用它承认故障存在，却不声称它持续不断或可稳定复现。

senses.title: Deliberate understatement
senses.definition: used to make a frequent habit sound rarer than it is
senses.definitionCN: 用来把频繁的习惯说得比实际更稀少
senses.example: He occasionally drinks more than he should.
senses.exampleCN: 他偶尔会喝得超过应有的量。
senses.why: The choice of a low-frequency word can soften a description that the facts would support more strongly.
senses.whyCN: 选用低频率的词可以软化描述，而事实本可支持更强的说法。

senses.title: As an exception
senses.definition: used of a case that departs from the usual rule
senses.definitionCN: 用于偏离通常规则的情形
senses.example: Permission is occasionally granted for late applications.
senses.exampleCN: 逾期申请偶尔会获得许可。
senses.why: The word marks the exception that proves the rule, keeping the general statement intact.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标出「证明规则」的例外，从而保住一般性说法。

senses.title: In older formal prose
senses.definition: in literary or dated writing, a refined substitute for sometimes
senses.definitionCN: 在文学或旧式文字中，作为「有时」的雅致替代
senses.example: The lake is occasionally visited by migrating birds.
senses.exampleCN: 这片湖泊间或有候鸟造访。
senses.why: The formal written use sounds more measured than sometimes and often appears in descriptive prose.
senses.whyCN: 正式书面用法比「有时」更有分寸，常见于描写性散文。

intro.en: Occasionally comes from the Latin verb for falling down or happening, through its noun and English adjective, plus the adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「落下、发生」的动词，经名词与英语形容词，再加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The verb cadere means to fall, as in a falling event.
items.cn: 动词意为「落下」，如事件降临。

items.en: The prefix ob-, meaning towards or upon, plus cadere gives occidere, to fall upon or set.
items.cn: 表示「朝向、落在」的前缀与「落下」合成「落到……上、沉降」。

items.en: The noun occasio names a chance that falls at one's feet, hence an occasion or opportunity.
items.cn: 名词指落到脚边的机会，也就是时机、场合。

items.en: English occasion comes through French and gives the adjective occasional, meaning happening now and then.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入「场合」，并派生形容词，意为「偶尔发生的」。

items.en: The adverb adds the usual suffix; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 副词加常见后缀；英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: Modern usage places the adverb below sometimes on the scale of frequency.
items.cn: 现代用法把它排在频率刻度上低于「有时」的位置。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin falling-root, including a look-alike from a different root; the second group orders expressions of frequency.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「落下」词根，其中包括一个形近但不同源的词；第二组按频率排列近义说法。

entries.definition: A particular time or event; the noun behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 特定的时刻或事件；副词背后的名词。

entries.definition: Happening from time to time; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 不时发生的；副词的形容词基形。

entries.definition: A philosophical view that events are caused directly by God on each occasion.
entries.definitionCN: 一种哲学观点，认为每次事件都由神直接引起。

entries.definition: Western; built on the Latin word for sunset, not on occasion.
entries.definitionCN: 西方的；由拉丁语「日落」构成，与「场合」无关。

entries.definition: On some occasions, more often than occasionally.
entries.definitionCN: 在某些场合，频率高于「偶尔」。

entries.definition: At intervals, without a fixed schedule.
entries.definitionCN: 间隔地，没有固定时间表。

entries.definition: A conversational phrase for an irregular low frequency.
entries.definitionCN: 口语短语，表示不规律的低频率。

entries.definition: In scattered, unpredictable instances.
entries.definitionCN: 以零散、不可预测的零星方式。

entries.definition: Stopping and starting again, often of a physical process.
entries.definitionCN: 断断续续地，多用于物理过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real falling-root and the real position of the word on the frequency scale.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「落下」词根，以及这个词在频率刻度上的真实位置。

normal.en: The root means to fall, so the event drops in now and then rather than on schedule.
normal.cn: 词根意为「落下」，所以事件是不定时掉进来，而不是按日程来。

normal.en: It sits below sometimes and far below often on the ladder of frequency.
normal.cn: 在频率阶梯上，它低于「有时」，远低于「经常」。

normal.en: Said first, it warns the listener that the next event is an exception.
normal.cn: 放在句首，它提醒听者接下来的事件只是例外。

normal.en: In a technical report it keeps a fault real without making it constant.
normal.cn: 在技术报告里，它让故障真实存在，却不把它说成持续不断。

normal.en: Used of a habit, it can politely make the habit sound rarer than it is.
normal.cn: 用于习惯时，它可以礼貌地把习惯说得比实际更稀少。

abstract.en: Occasionally is the word for the pattern that has no pattern.
abstract.cn: 「偶尔」是给「没有规律」的规律准备的词。

abstract.en: A low-frequency word is a dimmer switch for how much the listener should worry.
abstract.cn: 低频词像一个调光开关，控制听者该担心多少。

abstract.en: The exception needs a name so that the rule can stay standing.
abstract.cn: 例外需要一个名字，规则才能继续站着。

examples.en: The system occasionally restarts on its own.
examples.cn: 系统偶尔会自行重启。

examples.en: Occasionally, the lake freezes over completely.
examples.cn: 偶尔，湖面会完全封冻。

examples.en: She occasionally writes to the local paper.
examples.cn: 她偶尔给当地报纸投稿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「偶开胜利」——偶尔才开一次，不是常常

root: 拉丁语动词「落下」加表示「朝向」的前缀构成「落到……上、发生」，名词指落到脚边的时机；英语经法语借入名词并派生形容词「偶尔的」，再加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate low frequency, the sentence-opening frame, irregular intervals, relaxed speech, technical sporadicity, deliberate understatement, exception marking and older formal prose.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理低频、句首框架、不规则间隔、轻松口语、技术上的偶发、有意轻描淡写、标出例外，以及旧式书面用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a calendar with a few small circles and mostly empty days.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历上零星画着几个小圈，多数日子空白。

branches.en: THE LOW RATE: less often than sometimes.
branches.cn: 低频率：比「有时」更少。

branches.en: THE UNEVEN PATTERN: the opening frame and the irregular interval.
branches.cn: 不均匀的模式：句首框架与不规则间隔。

branches.en: THE SOFT HABIT: the relaxed spoken way to describe a loose routine.
branches.cn: 柔和的习惯：口语中描述松散日常的方式。

branches.en: THE MANAGED CLAIM: technical sporadicity and deliberate understatement.
branches.cn: 被管理的说法：技术上的偶发与有意的轻描淡写。

branches.en: THE EXCEPTION: a departure from the rule, and the older formal tone.
branches.cn: 例外：对规则的偏离，以及较旧的正式语气。

intro.en: Occasionally is a Latin towards-prefix, a falling-root, a noun of occasion, an English adjective and an English adverb suffix.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「朝向」前缀、「落下」词根、表「时机」的名词、英语形容词与英语副词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The root cadere is about falling; the prefixed verb names what falls upon a person, and the noun turns that into an occasion.
latinIntro.cn: 词根的核心是「落下」；加前缀的动词指落到某人身上的事，名词再把它变成「时机」。

items.example: The prefix points the falling toward a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「落下」指向某人。

items.example: The verb gives the family its image of an event arriving.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词为词族提供「事件降临」的意象。

items.example: The compound verb covers both happening and the setting sun.
items.exampleCN: 合成动词既指「发生」，也指「日落」。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a noun of occurrence.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成表「发生之事」的名词。

items.example: The noun names the chance that happens to arrive.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指恰好到来的机会。

items.example: English borrows the noun through French.
items.exampleCN: 英语经法语借入这个名词。

items.example: The adjective shifts the noun from an event to a frequency.
items.exampleCN: 形容词把名词从「事件」转向「频率」。

items.example: The philosophical noun keeps the idea of events falling on each occasion.
items.exampleCN: 这一哲学名词保留「每次场合事件降临」的观念。

items.example: The suffix turns occasional into a frequency adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成频率副词。

definition_en: especially, or in a way that singles out one part of a larger whole
core_image: 一排相同的灯泡里，有一盏被单独调亮
scene: 评审意见先谈整体，再把问题指向其中一处细节。The review praised the design, particularly the door handles.
sceneCN: 这里指从整体中单举一项（第 2 个义项：具体到某一项）；句意是评论称赞了设计，尤其是门把手。

senses.title: Especially in degree
senses.definition: more than usual or more than others in degree
senses.definitionCN: 在程度上超过平常或超过其他
senses.example: The winter was particularly harsh in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 北方的冬天格外严酷。
senses.why: Modifying an adjective, it raises the degree and invites a comparison with other times or places.
senses.whyCN: 修饰形容词时，它抬高程度，并引出与其他时间或地点的比较。

senses.title: In particular
senses.definition: used to single out one part of a larger whole
senses.definitionCN: 用来从较大的整体中单举一部分
senses.example: The report discusses costs, particularly labour costs.
senses.exampleCN: 报告讨论了成本，尤其是人力成本。
senses.why: Here the word narrows a general category to one member, close to specifically.
senses.whyCN: 这里它把一般类别收窄到某一成员，接近「具体地」。

senses.title: Sentence-opening emphasis
senses.definition: placed first to announce the most striking fact
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，宣布最引人注目的事实
senses.example: Particularly striking was the silence in the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 特别引人注目的是大厅里的沉默。
senses.why: The front position turns the highlighted element into the sentence's point of arrival.
senses.whyCN: 句首位置把被强调的成分变成整句的落点。

senses.title: Not particularly
senses.definition: used with not to lower a quality in a polite understatement
senses.definitionCN: 与否定词连用，礼貌地压低某种性质
senses.example: I am not particularly interested in that offer.
senses.exampleCN: 我对那个提议不太感兴趣。
senses.why: The negated form means less than very, a soft refusal rather than a plain no.
senses.whyCN: 否定形式意为「不到很的程度」，是柔和拒绝，而不是直截了当的「不」。

senses.title: Especially given
senses.definition: used before a phrase that strengthens the reasons for a statement
senses.definitionCN: 放在强化理由的短语前
senses.example: The schedule is tight, particularly given the staff shortage.
senses.exampleCN: 日程很紧，尤其考虑到人手不足。
senses.why: The construction adds a factor that makes the claim more forceful, often in argument.
senses.whyCN: 这一结构补上一个使说法更有力的因素，常用于论证。

senses.title: Particularly where or when
senses.definition: used before a clause to mark the case in which a statement matters most
senses.definitionCN: 放在从句前，标出该说法最适用的情形
senses.example: The rule matters particularly when records are shared.
senses.exampleCN: 这条规则在记录被共享时尤其重要。
senses.why: The clause restricts the emphasis to a specific circumstance instead of the whole topic.
senses.whyCN: 从句把强调限制在特定情形上，而不是整个话题。

senses.title: Particularly + noun group
senses.definition: used to single out a group affected by a general statement
senses.definitionCN: 用来单举受一般性说法影响的某一群体
senses.example: The change will affect staff, particularly those near retirement.
senses.exampleCN: 这一改动会影响员工，尤其是临近退休的人。
senses.why: The pattern picks out the subset that carries the main burden.
senses.whyCN: 这一句式挑出承担主要影响的那一子集。

senses.title: Formal written emphasis
senses.definition: in formal prose, a more precise alternative to especially
senses.definitionCN: 在正式散文中，作为「尤其」更精确的替代
senses.example: The findings are particularly relevant to small clinics.
senses.exampleCN: 这些发现对小诊所尤其相关。
senses.why: Formal writing prefers the word when the emphasis is on a specific case rather than a general high degree.
senses.whyCN: 当强调落在具体情形而非一般的「很」时，正式文字更偏爱这个词。

intro.en: Particularly comes from the Latin word for a small part, through its adjective and French, plus the English adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「小部分」一词，经形容词与法语，再加英语副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The noun pars, stem part-, means a part or share.
items.cn: 名词词干意为「部分、份额」。

items.en: The diminutive particula means a small part or particle.
items.cn: 指小形式意为「小部分、微粒」。

items.en: The adjective particularis means belonging to a single part or case.
items.cn: 形容词意为「属于某一部分或个别情形的」。

items.en: English particular passes through French and means specific rather than general.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入，意为「特定的」而非「一般的」。

items.en: The adverb adds the usual suffix; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 副词加常见后缀；英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: Modern usage separates precise singling out from mere intensity, especially in formal prose.
items.cn: 现代用法把「精确单举」与「单纯加强」分开，正式散文尤其如此。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin small-part stem; the second group contrasts precise singling out with broader degree intensifiers.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「小部分」词干；第二组对照「精确单举」与更宽泛的程度加强词。

entries.definition: Specific rather than general; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 特定而非一般的；副词的形容词基形。

entries.definition: The quality of being specific or detailed.
entries.definitionCN: 特定或详尽的性质。

entries.definition: To state something item by item.
entries.definitionCN: 逐项说明某事。

entries.definition: A very small piece; the same diminutive stem without the adjective ending.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的碎片；同一指小词干，未加形容词词尾。

entries.definition: Above all, or to a high degree; broader because it can simply intensify.
entries.definitionCN: 首先、格外；更宽，因为它可以单纯加强程度。

entries.definition: In a precise and identified way, without the degree sense.
entries.definitionCN: 以精确、指明的方式，不含程度义。

entries.definition: In a way worth noticing; often highlights an example or visible degree.
entries.definitionCN: 以值得注意的方式；常突出例子或可见程度。

entries.definition: The phrase form that singles out one member of a group.
entries.definitionCN: 单举群体中某一成员的短语形式。

entries.definition: More than everything else, ranking first in importance.
entries.definitionCN: 超过其他一切，在重要性上排第一。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real small-part stem and the real split between precision and intensity.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「小部分」词干，并区分「精确」与「强度」。

normal.en: The root is a small part, so the word pulls one piece out of the whole.
normal.cn: 词根是「小部分」，所以它从整体里拉出一块。

normal.en: The report discusses costs, particularly labour costs: that is the word doing its precise work.
normal.cn: 「报告讨论成本，尤其是人力成本」正是这个词在精确单举。

normal.en: Not particularly is a polite way to say not very, not a flat no.
normal.cn: 「不太」是礼貌地说「不是很」，而不是硬邦邦的拒绝。

normal.en: Particularly given adds a reason that makes the claim heavier.
normal.cn: 「尤其考虑到」补上一个让说法更重的理由。

normal.en: In formal prose it often replaces especially when the point is a specific case.
normal.cn: 正式文字里，当重点是具体情形时，它常替代「尤其」。

abstract.en: To be particular is to refuse the comfort of a general statement.
abstract.cn: 「具体」就是拒绝一般性说法带来的舒适。

abstract.en: A bright single lamp changes a row of identical lamps into a picture with a subject.
abstract.cn: 一盏单独调亮的灯，把一排相同的灯变成有主体的画面。

abstract.en: Precision and intensity are different tools, and the word can be either one.
abstract.cn: 精确与强度是两种不同的工具，而这个词两样都能当。

examples.en: The north is particularly cold in January.
examples.cn: 北方在一月格外寒冷。

examples.en: I am not particularly fond of crowded trains.
examples.cn: 我不太喜欢拥挤的火车。

examples.en: The rule was written particularly for small firms.
examples.cn: 这条规则尤其是为小公司写的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「怕提扣了利」——特别怕漏掉某一项，所以单独点出来

root: 拉丁语名词「部分」加指小后缀成「小部分」，再构成形容词「属于个别情形的」；英语经法语借入形容词后加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate degree emphasis, precise singling out, sentence-opening emphasis, negated understatement, added reasons, restricted circumstances, singled-out groups and formal written emphasis.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理程度加强、精确单举、句首强调、否定式低调、补充理由、限定情形、单举群体，以及正式书面强调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one lamp in a row turned brighter than all the rest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排相同的灯泡里，有一盏被单独调亮。

branches.en: THE DEGREE: more than usual or more than others.
branches.cn: 程度：超过平常或超过其他。

branches.en: THE SINGLED ITEM: one part of a whole, and one affected group.
branches.cn: 单举项：整体中的一部分，以及受影响的某一群体。

branches.en: THE FRONT POSITION: emphasis placed at the head of the sentence.
branches.cn: 前置位置：放在句首的强调。

branches.en: THE SOFT OR STRENGTHENED CLAIM: not particularly lowers, particularly given raises.
branches.cn: 柔化或加强的说法：「不太」压低，「尤其考虑到」抬高。

branches.en: THE RESTRICTED CASE: a circumstance clause and the formal register of precision.
branches.cn: 受限情形：限定情形的从句，以及精确的正式语域。

intro.en: Particularly is a Latin part-noun, a diminutive suffix, an adjective suffix, a French layer and an English adverb suffix.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「部分」名词、指小后缀、形容词后缀、法语层与英语副词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The noun for a part builds a diminutive for a small part, then an adjective for what belongs to one case.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「部分」的名词先构成「小部分」的指小形式，再构成「属于个别情形」的形容词。

items.example: The noun is the general idea of a piece of a whole.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是「整体中的一块」这一总概念。

items.example: The suffix shrinks a part into a small piece.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「部分」缩成小块。

items.example: The small part is the base of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 「小部分」是形容词的基词。

items.example: The suffix turns the small part into an adjective of belonging.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「小部分」变成表归属的形容词。

items.example: The adjective separates one case from the general class.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词把个别情形从一般类别中分出。

items.example: English keeps the adjective for a precise case.
items.exampleCN: 英语保留这个形容词指精确的个别情形。

items.example: The noun names the quality of being specific.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名「具体」这一性质。

items.example: The verb turns precision into an action.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把「精确」变成动作。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into an emphasis adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成强调副词。

definition_en: as may reasonably be supposed from the available evidence
core_image: 桌上的伞还在滴水，主人却不在，读者据此猜他刚回来
scene: 实验室的门锁着，灯却亮着，同事据此推断有人来过。The lights are on, so someone is presumably still inside.
sceneCN: 这里指根据迹象作出的合理推测（第 1 个义项：据推测）；句意为灯还亮着，所以想必里面还有人。

senses.title: As one may reasonably suppose
senses.definition: used to state what may reasonably be believed from the available evidence
senses.definitionCN: 说明根据现有证据可以合理相信的内容
senses.example: Presumably, the train was delayed by the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 据推测，火车是被暴风雨耽误了。
senses.why: The adverb presents an inference, not a fact: the speaker expects the listener to accept the reasoning.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词呈现的是推断而非事实：说话者期待听者接受这套推理。

senses.title: Probably, but unconfirmed
senses.definition: used of a likely fact that has not been checked
senses.definitionCN: 指很可能成立却尚未核实的事实
senses.example: The keys are presumably in the drawer.
senses.exampleCN: 钥匙想必在抽屉里。
senses.why: The word marks probability resting on a normal expectation rather than on proof.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标记的是建立在通常预期上的可能性，而不是证据。

senses.title: Sentence-opening inference
senses.definition: at the start of a sentence, presenting a conclusion drawn from what precedes
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，呈现由前文推出的结论
senses.example: Presumably, the author meant a different example.
senses.exampleCN: 想必作者想说的是另一个例子。
senses.why: The initial position frames the whole clause as a reader's inference, common in commentary.
senses.whyCN: 句首位置把整个小句框成读者的推断，这在评注文字中很常见。

senses.title: Presumably because
senses.definition: used to offer a likely explanation for something
senses.definitionCN: 用来为某事提出一个很可能的解释
senses.example: Presumably because of the rain, the match was cancelled.
senses.exampleCN: 想必是因为下雨，比赛被取消了。
senses.why: The pattern assigns a probable cause without claiming direct knowledge of it.
senses.whyCN: 这一句式给出可能的成因，却不声称直接知道它。

senses.title: Presumably not
senses.definition: used with not to state a likely negative conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 与否定词连用，说出一个很可能的否定结论
senses.example: Presumably not everyone agreed with the decision.
senses.exampleCN: 想必并非人人都同意这个决定。
senses.why: Negation keeps the hedging: the speaker infers a negative rather than asserting it.
senses.whyCN: 否定保留了缓冲：说话者是在推断一个否定，而不是断言。

senses.title: Hedging in academic prose
senses.titleCN: 学术写作中的推测语气
senses.definition: in scholarship, a courteous way to attribute an unstated intention to an author
senses.definitionCN: 在学术写作中，礼貌地把未明说的意图归给作者
senses.example: The passage is presumably an allusion to an older text.
senses.exampleCN: 这段文字想必是在暗指一部更早的文本。
senses.why: The hedge protects the writer from overclaiming about another person's meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这一缓冲保护作者，免得对他人的意思说得过满。

senses.title: Legal presumption
senses.definition: in law, describing a fact treated as true unless it is rebutted
senses.definitionCN: 在法律中，指除非被反驳否则视为真实的事实
senses.example: A person is presumably innocent until the case is proved.
senses.exampleCN: 在案件被证实之前，一个人被推定无罪。
senses.why: Legal usage turns the adverb into a rule about the burden of proof, not a casual guess.
senses.whyCN: 法律用法把这个副词变成关于举证责任的规则，而不是随口猜测。

senses.title: Ironic dismissal
senses.definition: in speech, used ironically to suggest that something is only supposedly true
senses.definitionCN: 在口语中反讽地表示某事只是「据说」成立
senses.example: Presumably, that explanation satisfies everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 想必这个解释能让所有人满意吧。
senses.why: The ironic tone leans on the word's hedging: the speaker repeats a claim while doubting it.
senses.whyCN: 反讽语气借用了这个词的缓冲：说话者重复一个说法，同时表示怀疑。

intro.en: Presumably comes from the Latin verb for taking beforehand, through its noun and English adjective, plus the adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「预先拿取」的动词，经名词与英语形容词，再加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The verb sumere means to take or take up.
items.cn: 动词意为「拿、取」。

items.en: The prefix prae- means before or in advance.
items.cn: 前缀意为「在前、预先」。

items.en: Praesumere means to take in advance, hence to assume or anticipate.
items.cn: 合成动词意为「预先拿走」，引申为「假定、预料」。

items.en: The noun praesumptio names an assumption taken beforehand.
items.cn: 名词指事先采取的假定。

items.en: English presume and presumable come through French and law; the adverb adds the usual suffix.
items.cn: 英语经法语与法学传统借入「假定」及其形容词，副词再加常见后缀。

items.en: Modern prose uses the adverb as a polite hedge in inference and academic commentary; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 现代散文用它作推断与学术评论中的礼貌缓冲；英语首见年代为约数。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin take-beforehand family, including a word with a stronger negative sense; the second group contrasts inference from evidence with plain probability.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「预先拿取」词族，其中包括一个贬义更强的词；第二组对照「由证据推断」与「单纯的可能性」。

entries.definition: To suppose something to be true before proof; also to dare without permission.
entries.definitionCN: 在证据前就假定为真；也指未经许可擅自。

entries.definition: An assumption taken as true, or behaviour that goes too far.
entries.definitionCN: 被视为真的假定，或越界的行为。

entries.definition: Able to be supposed; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 可以推定的；副词的形容词基形。

entries.definition: Going beyond what one has the right to do; the negative branch of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 越出本分、冒昧的；词族的贬义分支。

entries.definition: In all likelihood, without necessarily resting on a stated chain of evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 很可能，但不一定建立在明说的证据链上。

entries.definition: A formal phrase meaning very probably.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「很可能」的正式短语。

entries.definition: According to the normal course of things.
entries.definitionCN: 按照事情的通常走向。

entries.definition: Certainly or very probably; a stronger and older word.
entries.definitionCN: 确实或很可能；更强、更旧的词。

entries.definition: As it appears from what is seen or reported, without proof.
entries.definitionCN: 从所见或所闻看来如此，但未经证实。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real take-beforehand root and the real difference between inference and plain probability.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「预先拿取」词根，并区分「推断」与「单纯可能」。

normal.en: The root means to take beforehand, so the speaker takes a conclusion before the proof arrives.
normal.cn: 词根意为「预先拿取」，所以说话者在证据到之前先把结论拿来。

normal.en: The lights are on, so someone is presumably inside: evidence first, conclusion second.
normal.cn: 灯亮着，所以想必有人在里面：先有迹象，再有结论。

normal.en: Presumably because does the same work as probably because, but sounds more careful.
normal.cn: 「想必是因为」与「很可能是因为」作用相同，但听起来更谨慎。

normal.en: In academic prose it lets a writer guess at an author's intention without claiming to know it.
normal.cn: 在学术文字里，它让作者猜测原作者意图，却不声称知道。

normal.en: In law, presumably innocent is a rule about who must prove what.
normal.cn: 在法律里，「推定无罪」是一条关于谁来举证的规定。

abstract.en: To presume is to lend a fact before it has earned trust.
abstract.cn: 推测就是在一件事尚未赢得信任之前先借给它。

abstract.en: The hedge keeps the door open in case the inference turns out wrong.
abstract.cn: 缓冲把门留着，以防推断最后错了。

abstract.en: Irony here works by repeating a claim with the doubt left showing at the edges.
abstract.cn: 这里的反讽靠重复一个说法，却让怀疑留在边缘。

examples.en: Presumably, the meeting was moved because of the holiday.
examples.cn: 想必会议是因为假日而改期。

examples.en: The document is presumably a copy, not the original.
examples.cn: 这份文件想必是副本，而不是原件。

examples.en: Presumably not all the guests were invited.
examples.cn: 想必并非所有客人都受到了邀请。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普瑞祖母布里」——祖母凭经验猜，大概如此

root: 拉丁语动词「拿取」加表示「预先」的前缀，构成「预先拿走、假定」，其名词指事先采取的假定；英语经法语与法学传统借入动词与形容词，再加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate evidence-based inference, unconfirmed probability, sentence-opening inference, likely explanation, negated inference, academic hedging, legal presumption and ironic doubt.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理据证推断、未证实的可能、句首推断、可能解释、否定推断、学术缓冲、法律推定，以及反讽怀疑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dripping umbrella on the table while its owner is missing, so the reader guesses he just came in.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上的伞还在滴水，主人却不在，读者据此猜他刚进来。

branches.en: THE INFERENCE: evidence leads to a conclusion, whether inside the sentence or at its head.
branches.cn: 推断：证据引出结论，无论在句中还是句首。

branches.en: THE UNCHECKED FACT: likely by normal expectation, not proved.
branches.cn: 未核事实：按通常预期很可能，却未获证明。

branches.en: THE LIKELY CAUSE: a probable explanation offered without direct knowledge.
branches.cn: 可能成因：在没有直接知识时给出的合理解释。

branches.en: THE HEDGE: negated inference and the courteous academic buffer.
branches.cn: 缓冲：否定式推断与学术上的礼貌缓冲。

branches.en: THE RULE AND THE IRONY: legal burden of proof and the sceptical repeat.
branches.cn: 规则与反讽：法律举证责任与带怀疑的重复。

intro.en: Presumably is a Latin before-prefix, a taking-root, a noun of assumption, an English adjective and an English adverb suffix.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「预先」前缀、「拿取」词根、表「假定」的名词、英语形容词与英语副词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The root is taking; the prefix puts the taking before the fact, which is exactly what an assumption does.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是「拿取」；前缀把拿取放在事实之前，这正是「假定」所做的事。

items.example: The prefix puts the action ahead of the evidence.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作放在证据之前。

items.example: The verb supplies the physical act of taking.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「拿取」的具体动作。

items.example: The compound verb turns taking early into assuming.
items.exampleCN: 合成动词把「提前拿」变成「假定」。

items.example: The suffix builds the noun of assumption.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表「假定」的名词。

items.example: The noun is the base of the English legal term.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是英语法律术语的基词。

items.example: English keeps both the thinking and the daring senses.
items.exampleCN: 英语同时保留「思考」与「大胆」两条义。

items.example: The noun carries the same double life.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词也带着同样的双重身份。

items.example: A different suffix pulls out the negative branch.
items.exampleCN: 另一个后缀拉出贬义分支。

items.example: The suffix turns presumable into a hedge adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成缓冲副词。

definition_en: mainly, above all other things or purposes
core_image: 一栋房子的正门，旁边还有几扇小侧门
scene: 这座城市的经济靠港口，其他行业规模都小得多。The city's economy is primarily dependent on the port.
sceneCN: 这里指首要、占主导（第 1 个义项：主要地）；句意为这座城市的经济主要依赖港口。

senses.title: Mainly
senses.definition: for the most part, more than any other thing
senses.definitionCN: 大部分情况下，超过任何其他事物
senses.example: The book is primarily about language.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书主要讲语言。
senses.why: The word ranks one element above the rest without denying that others exist.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把某一要素排在其余之上，却不否认其余要素存在。

senses.title: First in responsibility
senses.definition: used of the person or body with the main duty
senses.definitionCN: 用于承担主要职责的人或机构
senses.example: The committee is primarily responsible for safety.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会对安全负主要责任。
senses.why: Here the word concerns rank of obligation, not frequency or quantity.
senses.whyCN: 这里它说的是责任的等级，而不是频率或数量。

senses.title: Primarily because
senses.definition: used to name the main reason among several
senses.definitionCN: 用来在多个原因中指出主要那一个
senses.example: He resigned primarily because of ill health.
senses.exampleCN: 他辞职主要是因为健康不佳。
senses.why: The causal pattern admits other reasons while naming the dominant one.
senses.whyCN: 这一因果句式承认还有其他原因，同时点出主导原因。

senses.title: Primarily for a purpose
senses.definition: of a thing, intended first of all for one use
senses.definitionCN: 指某物的首要用途
senses.example: The land is used primarily for farming.
senses.exampleCN: 这片土地主要用于耕作。
senses.why: The word identifies the main function, leaving other uses as secondary.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指出主要功能，把其他用途留作次要。

senses.title: Primarily designed to
senses.definition: used before a verb of design or purpose to state the main aim
senses.definitionCN: 放在设计或目的动词前，说明主要目标
senses.example: The tool is primarily designed to cut wood.
senses.exampleCN: 这件工具的首要设计目的是切木头。
senses.why: Technical descriptions use the word to separate the intended function from incidental ones.
senses.whyCN: 技术说明用它把预期功能与附带功能分开。

senses.title: Primarily aimed at
senses.definition: of a course or product, intended mainly for one group
senses.definitionCN: 指课程或产品主要面向某一群体
senses.example: The programme is primarily aimed at beginners.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目主要面向初学者。
senses.why: The pattern states the target audience and implies that others are not the main concern.
senses.whyCN: 这一句式说明目标受众，并暗示其他人不是主要考虑。

senses.title: Formal register for mainly
senses.definition: in formal prose, a heavier alternative to mainly
senses.definitionCN: 在正式散文中，作为「主要」的较重替代
senses.example: The decline is primarily due to changes in demand.
senses.exampleCN: 这一下降主要归因于需求变化。
senses.why: Formal writing prefers the word when the claim carries weight in an argument.
senses.whyCN: 当论断在论证中有分量时，正式文字更偏爱这个词。

senses.title: Primarily concerned with
senses.definition: used of a field or text, focused on one subject above others
senses.definitionCN: 指某领域或文本把某一主题置于其他之上
senses.example: The chapter is primarily concerned with ethics.
senses.exampleCN: 这一章主要关注伦理问题。
senses.why: The phrase describes the centre of attention, often in academic summaries.
senses.whyCN: 这一短语描述注意力的中心，常用于学术摘要。

intro.en: Primarily comes from the Latin adjective for first in rank, through English primary, plus the adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「第一等级」的形容词，经英语形容词「首要的」，再加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The adjective primus means first in order or rank.
items.cn: 形容词意为「在次序或等级上第一的」。

items.en: The adjective primarius means of the first rank or chief.
items.cn: 形容词意为「第一等级的、首要的」。

items.en: English primary comes through French and means first in importance as well as first in order.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入，既指次序最先，也指重要性居首。

items.en: The adverb adds the usual suffix; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 副词加常见后缀；英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: Modern usage ranks importance and purpose rather than strict temporal order.
items.cn: 现代用法排的是重要性与目的，而不是严格的时间先后。

items.en: The adverb settles in formal and technical prose as a stronger mainly.
items.cn: 这个副词在正式与技术散文中定型，语气比「主要地」更重。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin first-rank family; the second group contrasts main importance with leading rank or plain majority.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「第一等级」词族；第二组对照「主要重要性」与「首领地位」或「单纯多数」。

entries.definition: First in importance or order; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 在重要性或次序上第一的；副词的形容词基形。

entries.definition: The state of being first in rank or authority.
entries.definitionCN: 在等级或权威上居首的状态。

entries.definition: First in quality or importance; also the period of greatest strength.
entries.definitionCN: 在质量或重要性上居首；也指最强盛的时期。

entries.definition: Belonging to the earliest or most basic level.
entries.definitionCN: 属于最早或最基础层面的。

entries.definition: For the most part; the plainer everyday counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 大部分情况下；更朴素的日常对应词。

entries.definition: Above all others, often ranking rather than measuring.
entries.definitionCN: 超过其他一切，常偏重等级而非数量。

entries.definition: To a great extent, often of proportions.
entries.definitionCN: 在很大程度上，常指比例。

entries.definition: Chiefly, with a heavier formal and institutional tone.
entries.definitionCN: 主要地，带更重的正式与机构语气。

entries.definition: More than everything else, with clear ranking.
entries.definitionCN: 超过其他一切，带明确的排序。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real first-rank family and the real split between main importance and leading rank.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「第一等级」词族，并区分「主要重要性」与「首领地位」。

normal.en: The root means first, so the word puts one item at the front of the line.
normal.cn: 词根意为「第一」，所以它把某一项排到队伍最前。

normal.en: Primarily responsible is about duty, not frequency.
normal.cn: 「负主要责任」说的是职责，不是频率。

normal.en: Primarily because names the leading reason and lets the others stand behind it.
normal.cn: 「主要因为」点出主导原因，让其他原因站在后面。

normal.en: Primarily aimed at identifies the audience the maker had in mind.
normal.cn: 「主要面向」指明制作者心里的受众。

normal.en: Formal prose uses it where mainly would sound too light for the claim.
normal.cn: 正式散文用它，因为「主要」对这份论断来说太轻。

abstract.en: Main importance is a ranking, and a ranking is a decision about what comes first.
abstract.cn: 主要性是一种排序，而排序就是决定什么排在最前。

abstract.en: A main door does not make the side doors unreal; it only decides where visitors enter.
abstract.cn: 正门并不让侧门变得不存在，它只决定客人从哪里进。

abstract.en: The word is a quiet way of saying that one reason outranks the rest.
abstract.cn: 这个词是安静地说：有一个理由压过其余。

examples.en: The region is primarily agricultural.
examples.cn: 这个地区主要从事农业。

examples.en: The delay was primarily caused by the weather.
examples.cn: 延误主要是天气造成的。

examples.en: The course is primarily intended for new staff.
examples.cn: 这门课程主要面向新员工。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普赖么瑞利」——排在第一排，主要就它

root: 拉丁语形容词「第一的」构成「第一等级的、首要的」，英语经法语借入形容词「主要的」，再加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate main importance, first responsibility, leading reason, main purpose, primary design aim, target audience, formal register and academic focus.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理主要重要性、首要责任、主导原因、主要用途、首要设计目的、目标受众、正式语域，以及学术关注点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the front door of a house, with several smaller side doors beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一栋房子的正门，旁边还有几扇小侧门。

branches.en: THE MAIN ELEMENT: more than any other thing.
branches.cn: 主要要素：超过任何其他事物。

branches.en: THE LEADING CLAIM: first responsibility and the dominant reason.
branches.cn: 领先的主张：首要责任与主导原因。

branches.en: THE INTENDED USE: main function and primary design aim.
branches.cn: 预期用途：主要功能与首要设计目的。

branches.en: THE AUDIENCE: the group the thing is mainly for.
branches.cn: 受众：该事物主要面向的群体。

branches.en: THE FORMAL CENTRE: heavier register and the focus of a field or text.
branches.cn: 正式中心：更重的语域，以及领域或文本的关注点。

intro.en: Primarily is a Latin first-adjective, its rank adjective, an English adjective and an English adverb suffix.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「第一」形容词、表等级的形容词、英语形容词与英语副词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The first word builds an adjective of first rank, and English draws primary, primacy and prime from the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「第一」的词构成「第一等级」的形容词，英语从同一词干取得「主要的」「首要地位」与「首要的」。

items.example: The adjective is the simple ranking word behind the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是词族背后最简单的排序词。

items.example: The suffix builds an adjective of rank.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表等级的形容词。

items.example: The adjective names those who stand at the head.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词指站在最前面的人。

items.example: English keeps both the ranking and the early-stage senses.
items.exampleCN: 英语同时保留「排序」与「早期阶段」两条义。

items.example: The noun names the position rather than the quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名位置，而不是性质。

items.example: The short form covers both rank and peak time.
items.exampleCN: 短形式同时覆盖等级与巅峰时期。

items.example: Another branch stresses earliness rather than rank.
items.exampleCN: 另一分支强调「最早」，而不是等级。

items.example: The suffix turns primary into a ranking adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成排序副词。

items.example: The adverb ranks importance in a whole statement.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词在整句范围内排定重要性。

definition_en: chiefly, above all other things or in the leading position
core_image: 一张圆桌上只有一个座位摆在正中，其余都在侧边
scene: 这家小公司做的是沿海运输，别的业务只是顺便。The small firm is principally engaged in coastal shipping.
sceneCN: 这里指正式文体中的主营活动（第 8 个义项：法律或金融文本中的「主要从事」）；句意为这家小公司主要从事沿海航运。

senses.title: Chiefly
senses.definition: for the most part, above all other things
senses.definitionCN: 大部分情况下，超过其他一切
senses.example: The region is principally agricultural.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区主要务农。
senses.why: The word ranks one activity above others, close to chiefly but heavier in tone.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把某项活动排在其余之上，接近「主要地」，但语气更重。

senses.title: First in importance
senses.definition: used of what matters most in a hierarchy
senses.definitionCN: 用于等级体系中最重要的事物
senses.example: The fund is principally for research, not buildings.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔基金主要用于研究，而不是建筑。
senses.why: Here the word ranks importance rather than quantity, often in institutional decisions.
senses.whyCN: 这里它排的是重要性而非数量，常见于机构决策。

senses.title: Principally because
senses.definition: used to name the dominant cause
senses.definitionCN: 用来指出主导原因
senses.example: The delay was principally due to a shortage of funds.
senses.exampleCN: 延误主要是资金短缺造成的。
senses.why: The causal pattern selects the leading reason and lets others remain in the background.
senses.whyCN: 这一因果句式挑出主导理由，让其他理由留在背景。

senses.title: Principally responsible for
senses.definition: used of the agent with the leading duty
senses.definitionCN: 用于承担首要职责的主体
senses.example: The ministry is principally responsible for the policy.
senses.exampleCN: 该部门对这项政策负主要责任。
senses.why: The phrase assigns responsibility at the top of an institutional chain.
senses.whyCN: 这一短语把责任放在机构链条的最上层。

senses.title: Principally concerned with
senses.definition: used of a text or field focused on one question
senses.definitionCN: 指文本或领域聚焦于某一问题
senses.example: The chapter is principally concerned with property rights.
senses.exampleCN: 这一章主要涉及财产权。
senses.why: Academic summaries use the phrase to state the centre of a discussion.
senses.whyCN: 学术摘要用这一短语说明讨论的中心。

senses.title: Principally used for
senses.definition: of a place or object, serving one main function
senses.definitionCN: 指场所或物品承担一项主要功能
senses.example: The hall is principally used for concerts.
senses.exampleCN: 这个大厅主要用于音乐会。
senses.why: The pattern states the main function and leaves other uses as exceptions.
senses.whyCN: 这一句式说明主要功能，把其他用途留作例外。

senses.title: Principally aimed at
senses.definition: of a measure, intended to affect one group or problem
senses.definitionCN: 指措施意在影响某一群体或问题
senses.example: The tax is principally aimed at large estates.
senses.exampleCN: 这项税主要针对大型地产。
senses.why: Policy writing uses the word to identify the main target of an instrument.
senses.whyCN: 政策写作借此词指出一项工具的主要目标。

senses.title: Formal and legal main activity
senses.definition: in legal or financial prose, describing the main business of a company
senses.definitionCN: 在法律或金融文字中描述公司的主要业务
senses.example: The company is principally engaged in coastal shipping.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司主要从事沿海航运。
senses.why: The fixed legal phrase marks the core activity, a use where the word's formality is strongest.
senses.whyCN: 这一固定法律短语标记核心业务，是这个词正式感最强的用法。

intro.en: Principally comes from the Latin adjective for belonging to the chief, built on the words for first and take, plus the English adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「属于首领的」形容词，其词根由「第一」与「拿取」构成，再加英语副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The adjective primus means first.
items.cn: 形容词意为「第一的」。

items.en: The verb capere means to take or seize.
items.cn: 动词意为「拿取、抓取」。

items.en: The noun princeps, first taker, means the leading person; its stem princip- supplies the adjective.
items.cn: 名词字面「首先拿取者」，指首领；其词干提供形容词。

items.en: The adjective principalis means belonging to the chief or first rank.
items.cn: 形容词意为「属于首领或首位的」。

items.en: English principal comes through French and means chief or main, as adjective and noun.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入，作形容词与名词都表「首要的、负责人」。

items.en: The adverb adds the usual suffix and settles in formal, legal and financial prose; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 副词加常见后缀，定居于正式、法律与金融文体；英语首见年代为约数。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin chief-stem, including two words often confused; the second group contrasts leading rank with main importance or plain majority.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「首领」词干，其中包括两个常被混淆的词；第二组对照「首领地位」与「主要重要性」或「单纯多数」。

entries.definition: Chief or main; also the head of a school or a sum of money.
entries.definitionCN: 首要的、主要的；也指校长或本金。

entries.definition: A rule or basic truth; it comes from the beginning-branch of the same stem, not from principal.
entries.definitionCN: 规则或基本原理；来自同一词干的「开端」分支，而非「首要的」那一支。

entries.definition: A royal son or ruler of a small state, from the same first-taker noun.
entries.definitionCN: 王子或小国统治者，来自同一个「首先拿取者」名词。

entries.definition: A small state ruled by a prince.
entries.definitionCN: 由亲王统治的小国；公国。

entries.definition: Above all others, with a neutral tone.
entries.definitionCN: 超过其他一切，语气中性。

entries.definition: For the most part; the plain everyday choice.
entries.definitionCN: 大部分情况下；日常最朴素的选择。

entries.definition: Mainly, with emphasis on first-order importance or purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 主要地，强调第一序的重要性或目的。

entries.definition: More than everything else, with explicit ranking.
entries.definitionCN: 超过其他一切，带明确排序。

entries.definition: For the most part, allowing exceptions.
entries.definitionCN: 大体上，允许例外。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real first-taker root and the real split between leading rank and plain majority.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「首先拿取者」词根，并区分「首领地位」与「单纯多数」。

normal.en: The root is first taker, so the word points to whoever or whatever stands at the head.
normal.cn: 词根是「首先拿取者」，所以这个词指向站在最前面的那个人或那件事。

normal.en: Principal and principle look identical but come from two branches: leader and beginning.
normal.cn: 「负责人」与「原理」拼写相同，却来自两条分支：首领与开端。

normal.en: Principally engaged in is the legal way to name a company's core business.
normal.cn: 「主要从事」是法律上命名公司核心业务的说法。

normal.en: Principally responsible puts the duty at the top of the chain.
normal.cn: 「负主要责任」把职责放在链条顶端。

normal.en: In formal prose it sounds heavier than mainly, which is the point.
normal.cn: 在正式散文里它比「主要地」更重，这正是它的用处。

abstract.en: A principal seat is central not because it is bigger, but because the table is arranged around it.
abstract.cn: 主位之所以居中，不是因为椅子更大，而是因为桌子围着它摆。

abstract.en: Leadership is a rank, while main importance is a weight; the word can lean either way.
abstract.cn: 首领是一种等级，主要性是一种分量；这个词两边都能靠。

abstract.en: Formality here is a way of making a ranking sound like a fact.
abstract.cn: 这里的正式感，是把排序说得像事实的一种方式。

examples.en: The island is principally known for its birds.
examples.cn: 这座岛主要以鸟类闻名。

examples.en: The scheme is principally funded by the central government.
examples.cn: 这项计划主要由中央政府出资。

examples.en: The chapter is principally about the early years of the project.
examples.cn: 这一章主要讲项目的早期年份。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普林西普利」——首领坐正位，事情主要归他

root: 拉丁语「第一」与「拿取」合成名词「首先拿取者、首领」，其词干构成形容词「属于首领的」；英语经法语借入形容词「首要的」，再加副词后缀。「原理」一词来自同词干的另一分支「开端」，与本词同源不同义。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate chief activity, first importance, dominant cause, leading responsibility, academic focus, main function, policy target and the formal legal main business.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理主要活动、首要重要性、主导原因、首要责任、学术关注、主要功能、政策目标，以及正式法律文体中的主营。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round table with one seat at the centre and the rest along the side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张圆桌，只有一个座位在正中，其余都在侧边。

branches.en: THE HEAD PLACE: chief activity and first importance in a hierarchy.
branches.cn: 首位：主要活动与等级中的首要重要性。

branches.en: THE LEADING REASON AND DUTY: dominant cause and top responsibility.
branches.cn: 主导理由与职责：主导原因与最高责任。

branches.en: THE ACADEMIC CENTRE: the question a text is mainly about.
branches.cn: 学术中心：文本主要讨论的问题。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT: main function and policy target.
branches.cn: 工具：主要功能与政策目标。

branches.en: THE FORMAL CORE BUSINESS: the legal phrase for a company's main activity.
branches.cn: 正式核心业务：用于公司主营的法律短语。

intro.en: Principally is a Latin first-word, a taking-root, a chief-noun, an adjective suffix and an English adverb suffix; the same stem also yields principle by a different branch.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「第一」、 「拿取」词根、表「首领」的名词、形容词后缀与英语副词后缀构成；同一词干经另一分支还产生「原理」。

latinIntro.en: The chief noun is literally first taker; its stem builds principal, while a beginning-branch builds principle.
latinIntro.cn: 表「首领」的名词字面是「首先拿取者」；其词干构成「首要的」，另一「开端」分支则构成「原理」。

items.example: The adjective supplies the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供合成词的前半。

items.example: The verb supplies the taking half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供合成词中「拿取」的那一半。

items.example: The noun names the person at the head of a group.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指群体最前面的那个人。

items.example: The suffix turns the chief noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「首领」名词变成形容词。

items.example: The adjective ranks a thing by its leading position.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词按首领地位为事物排序。

items.example: A different branch of the same stem gives the word for principle.
items.exampleCN: 同一词干的另一分支给出表「原理」的词。

items.example: English keeps the ranking sense in both adjective and noun.
items.exampleCN: 英语在形容词与名词中都保留排序义。

items.example: The look-alike comes from the beginning branch, not from principal.
items.exampleCN: 这个形近词来自「开端」分支，而不是来自「首要的」那一支。

items.example: The suffix turns principal into a ranking adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成排序副词。
